- Setup/Processing
- Limit Payment to MTM Additional Logic
- In Deal Setup > Other Settings, a new setting called "Limit payment to MTM" was added
- If enabled, iManage will only send payment details in MTM
- Background: There are deals that process monthly, but only pay quarterly (MTM).  For the non-payment months, we should not be sending payments/cash to VIPR or SDDB.
- Currently, this was only applied to automated deals.  The same logic will get applied to the legacy signoff process in the next release.
- Automatic Enabling of Auto Report Step
- If the Package Report step is optionally-enabled on the Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab, the Generate Auto Reports step will automatically be enabled with it
- Ex. A deal has the Bond Reporting template enabled, which the Package Report step is not a default step of.  If the deal team optionally enables the Package Report step, the Generate Auto Reports step should also be enabled because it is needed to generate the shell/component files of the package.
- Flag Setting With Calculate Expenses Workflow Step
- In Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow, if users enable the Calculate Expenses workflow step, iManage will check to see if Other Setting "Check expenses in tax range" has been enabled for the deal.  If not, it will automatically enable the setting.
- Note: If the step is disabled in the workflow, iManage will not remove the setting.  Users will manually have to remove.
- Approval / Workflow
- Duplicate DIDs in Incomplete Deals list
- In the My Deals screen, if the Show All option was enabled, deals would be listed twice for prior periods
- This bug has been fixed
- Duplicate Going Green Tasks Displayed
- For some deals, if the Check Report steps have to be re-run, the tasks would appear multiple times
- The reason was the form was not filtering tax tasks for the same deal
- In both legacy and automation workflows, this bug has been fixed so that only bond tasks are displayed during the Check Report steps
- Package Report Business Logic - Skip Excel Package
- If the “Skip Excel Package” Other Setting was enabled on the deal, system was correctly not creating the Excel version of the final package
- However, at the Package Report workflow step, it was incorrectly still looking for the Excel version of the final package
- The logic for the step was updated to check that setting and skip the file lookup, if enabled
- Step Should Fail If Import Fails
- If the import of the payment/tax range fails, the steps that does the import (Process Distrib, Package Reports, Processor Signoff, etc.) were not failing
- Eventually, workflow would fail at Processor Signoff due to the missing data, i.e. it’s unable to do the large wire check o However, that message did not guide users to the actual problem
- Now, if the payment/tax range import fails, the related step will fail – the earlier, the better
### If the import fails due to a mismatch in the payment or tax range name, the fail will state so:
- VIPR
- As deals are onboarded to VIPR, we have the opportunity to share data between the systems and catch mismatches before they become an issue on payment date
- New Other Setting
- When we get confirmation that a deal is now being processed in VIPR, IR needs to enable the “VIPR Import Payment Ready API” setting in Deal Setup > Other Settings for that deal
- At the same time, the deal must be flagged with the GSFIR Account Dimension in VIPR by the Account or Cash team
### At Reviewer/Looksee Signoff, if iManage flagged the deal, but it is not flagged in VIPR, the step will fail:
- It is important to flag the deal correctly so that the payments are sent to the right system o If deal is not yet in VIPR, payments must be sent to SDDB o If deal is in VIPR, payments must be sent to VIPR
### o If you get this error, work with the Cash Analyst on the deal and update the applicable flags in either system o This applies to legacy signoffs as well (for UK deals):
- Discrepancy Check Logic
- Once the deal is flagged in both systems, we will pull various setup fields for the deal every morning and compare those data points to what we have setup in iManage.
- Logic
### • Disparity checks will be done on the following fields:
- VIPR’s External System ID must match iManage’s PmtID exactly o VIPR’s External Series must match iManage’s PmtID exactly
- VIPR’s Class (name) must match iManage’s Class (name) from tblPmtInfo exactly ▪ Applies to active classes only
- Email Notifications
- If there are any mismatches in the above fields, a Discrepancy Report will be sent to GSF IR Support to start
- Once the process is confirmed to be working as expected, the report will instead be sent to IR for resolution o Expectation is that the IR deal team will work with the Cash team to correct whatever is necessary in either application
- Once the fields are updated as required, managers can rerun the discrepancy report from Reports to verify that the discrepancies were resolved
- Signoffs
- • If the discrepancies are not resolved by the time the deal is processed, the Reviewer/Looksee Signoff step will fail o If the External System ID in VIPR does not match the PmtID in iManage, the reports will not post on Pivot
- o If the External Series in VIPR does not match the PmtID in iManage, the payments will not flow to the deal in VIPR correctly o If the Class (name) in VIPR does not match the Class (name) in iManage, the payments for that class will not flow to VIPR correctly • Therefore, it is imperative to resolve any discrepancies before signing off on the deal
- Automatically Update Deal Contacts
- If iManage has different contacts assigned to the Account Administrator and Cash Analyst roles that what is found in VIPR, iManage will automatically update the contacts to match VIPR
- There will be no notification of the change
- If the contacts are wrong, they must be updated in VIPR and that will, in turn, update the contacts in iManage
- Possible Payments to Inactive Classes
- • At Reviewer/Looksee Signoff, if iManage shows that we are making payments [Prin and Int Dist] to a class that is not found in VIPR, we will allow the step to complete, but will also send an email notification to the necessary parties to investigate
- Payment Files/API
- If a deal is in VIPR and payments for the deal are approved, iManage will feed the class payments and cash events to VIPR in various ways
- If the deal is automated, iManage will feed the data to VIPR via an API o The Cash Analyst will still get the email notification regarding the payment approval, but it will state that the payments were loaded to VIPR
- As a failsafe, if the payments fail to load into VIPR for whatever reason, we are also sweeping the payment file to a new payment file (Archive) location created for VIPR
- This applies to whether the Reviewer/Looksee Signoff step is completed via legacy iManage, IREM or Portfolio View o If the step is reverted, the payments will automatically be pulled from VIPR
- If the deal still goes through the legacy signoff process, the payment file will sweep to the new payment file location created for VIPR
- If the deal is not yet in VIPR, payment files will continue to sweep to the old SDDB location

- Preliminary Statements Not Consistently Sweeping (Cash Analysts)
- Upon a successful Reviewer Signoff (in both legacy and automation processes), the Distribution Report is supposed to sweep to the X:\SFS Data Files\FSIR\Preliminary Statements folder
- Cash Analysts can pull the approved reports from that location for their reconciliation (days prior to when the deal is final delivered)
- However, since automation doesn’t have access to the X: drive, we use an Active Batch job to sweep the reports and the job would only try to sweep the files once
- o For whatever reason, the files often fail to get saved to the X: drive
- We have enhanced the Active Batch job to verify that the files make it to the X: drive and if not, to retry until they do

- The logic has been updated to only check on the current allocations of the deal and, if shelf-allocated, the shelf member’s role within the shelf

- System Resource Intensive (SRI) Deals
- Background
- There are some deals that take a long time to process collateral data and if they are run simultaneously, they can bring the database down or cause blocking
- For example, whenever multiple Lakeview or BVRT deals ran at the same time, everyone would experience very slow performance in iManage
- For years, Agency deals had to be processed systematically by an Active Batch job that ensured each deal ran sequentially so they wouldn’t cause the same issues o However, deal teams had no control over the processing and had to rely heavily on TOS support whenever anything went wrong
- New Solution
- To address these issues, TOS has created a new process that allows these deals to be processed by deal teams, but still run sequentially
- Applicable deals need be added to tblWorkflowSystemResourceIntensiveDeal (via the DMT) and must include a MaxWorkflowStep o The MaxWorkflowStep is the last WorkflowStepID (refer to the My Deals > Automation grid) that the deal runs while holding up the rest of the deals in the special queue
- If multiple of these deals are kicked off at the same time, the first one picked up by the queue will run through that deal’s MaxWorkflowStep while all the other deals wait in the queue o For example, if BVRT Series KiloNine-2 is picked up first, it will run through the Accept
- o
- Data workflow step before the next SRI deal in the queue can begin o Once Accept Data is complete, BVRT’s remaining workflow steps will keep processing while CSFB 2001-28’s workflow starts and so forth
- The queue is looking for SRI deals that are “InProg”.  Therefore, if the first SRI deal running fails at one of its steps, its status will change to “Fail” and the next SRI will get picked up.
- Automation Processing
- If there are no other SRIs running, you may run a SRI deal in Manual or Local Automation mode
- However, if there are other SRIs deals in the queue, you will be instructed to run the deal in Cloud Automation
- If there are other SRIs in the queue and you try to kick off the deal in Cloud mode, you will reminded that it has been added to the queue
- The Late Form at the Begin Workflow step will be skipped for SRIs since they should be run in Cloud mode (and users wouldn’t be able to run the step in Manual mode to fill out the form) o The Late Form will pop later at the Processor Signoff step
- If a SRI deal is running and you want to stop it from moving forward, you can hit the Stop button and it will complete the step it is currently on and then stop.  It will not keep processing through the deal’s MaxWorkflowStep. o This will also allow the next deal in the queue to start processing
- If you have a SRI deal waiting in the queue and want to remove it from the queue, you can also hit the Stop button and it should remove the deal from the queue

- Implement Backup Late Logic to Workflow Engine
### The following updated late logic has been integrated into Cloud Automation (as it was previously only implemented for Manual and Local Automation):
### For Bond and Fund Accounting deals:
- On/after Due Date, if after 5 p.m. CST, considered internal late o On Payment Date, if after 1 p.m. CST, considered external late
### For Backup Servicing and Global Duty deals:
- On/after Due Date, if after 6 p.m. CST, considered internal late o On Payment Date, if after 6 p.m. CST, considered external late
- As with any Cloud Automation fails, the email notification (for those who are opted in) will advise users that the late form must be completed
- DailyUnverifiedDistribReport
- There was a previous fix to update the Verifier dropdown in the Locking form to only include active employees
- However, if the user has multiple records in tblEmployee (left the bank and came back), the system was still incorrectly saving the Verifier using their old/inactive ID
- Due to this bug, the intended Verifier would never see the deals they need to verify because those records were saved under their old ID
- Now, only the active employee ID selected from the dropdown will be saved as the Verifier and thus, the deals will correctly appear in their view
- Reject Button on Verification only unlock the distrib
- When a Verifier rejects changes made to a distrib, the system would unlock the file, but there was no way to systematically let the Processor know that the issue was back on their plate (and no longer needing action by the Verifier)
- Now, upon rejection, an email notification will be sent to the Processor
- And the deal will be removed from the Verifier’s list

- Deliver Final Reports workflow step for Bond deals

### Currently the only sprocs available to be integrated into workflows are:
- spPreProcess_LoanIRR        spInsertLoanCF0_Transfer spPostProcess_CalcOID        spUpdateCalcIRR_Transfer spInsertRefiData            spUpdateCalcIRRTax_Transfer spInsertLoanCashflow        spInsertLoanCF0 spUpdateLoanYield            spUpdateCalcIRR spInsertLoanNPV            spUpdateCalcIRRTax spInsertLoanOID
- These sprocs are only available for Bond and Fund Accounting templates

- Remove Open Distrib From Setup

- o Note: If an Advanced Setting is enabled and there is an outstanding workflow being processed, you will get the warning that making the setup change will wipe out signoffs and reset the workflow
- FileID Enhancements
- Monitoring Folders for Files
- Enhancements have been implemented to FileID setup so that a user never has to get involved or click any buttons to find a source file, import or kick off the workflow.
- Enhanced File Monitoring Job
- The file monitoring job that checks to see if there are any overdue files will now run every day at 12 a.m./6 a.m./12 p.m./4 p.m. CST
- It will query Import File Setup and if it finds an outstanding file as defined in the File Default Location (with MapID 0), it will look for the file based on the Date Code you setup and during those four times on that date
- Note: If workflow has already started for the period, it will not look for the deal’s files for that period
- New Setup Fields
### The Import File Setup has been enhanced to allow users to optionally define the following for each FileID:
- How long to look for a file (Date Code + ## DaysAfter) before it’s considered overdue o When adding a Date Code, users can now set a number of calendar days after the optimal day they expect to receive a file
### ▪ For example, you usually get the periodic file between the 12th and 15th and you manually have to check a specific folder during those days for the file ▪ You can setup the Date Code as:
- The monitoring job will automatically look for the file in the source folder you defined in File Default Location during those days o After those days have passed, the file will be considered overdue and start appearing on the "Daily Overdue FileIDs" report so you know to follow up on the file
- If Days After is left blank, the monitoring job will only look for the file on the calculated date
- (based on the Date Code)
- If not found on that one day, file is considered overdue and the expectation is for you to follow up with the data provider for the file
- Once received, you must manually load the file
- Scrubber
- If the raw data you receive from the servicer needs to be run through a scrubber, the monitoring job can automatically queue up the scrubber once the source file is found
### Setup the FileID for the raw data file to include the following:
- Map = 0
- File Default Location = file path of the raw data file
- Date Code + Days After = the day(s) you expect to get the raw data file
- Scrubber = the ScrubTemplateName of the scrubber that is used on the file (limited to the scrubbers as defined in the ToolsHub library)
- If populated, on the expected days, the monitoring job will look for the file as defined in File
- Default Location
- Once found, it will add the file to the scrubbing queue
- The scrubber will output the final data file as defined in the Destination Folder field
- The destination file can then be used for your other FileIDs that use actual import maps
- Please refer to Enhancements to FileIDs (Web view) on other ways the Import File Setup can be used to manage files
- Cloud Automation Not Kicking Off with Hardcoded FileID
- Previously, if the last FileID that was loaded (via a loader) used a hardcoded map, automation workflow would not automatically kick off
- This bug is fixed now so that regardless of the map type, once the last FileID is loaded, workflow should automatically kick off
- Allocations

- For automated deals, if your allocations don’t sync up to the enabled workflow steps, the
- Allocation Managers will no longer be stopped when trying to assign deals o Instead, the check will now be done on the Begin Workflow step (details below)
- Add Check for Non-Automated Deals in Allocations
- There used to be a check during legacy signoff that would stop the process if a Reviewer is not assigned to a non-automated bond deal, but the check was unintentionally removed
- To ensure there is always a Reviewer, the check will now be done on the Allocations screen
- For non-automated bond deals, if user tries to assign a Reviewer to Not Avail, it will fail
- Allocation Check Update
- iManage will no longer check the selected deal assignments to the deal’s workflow steps to make sure they are in sync on the Allocations screen o Ex. Even if the Looksee – Signoff step is not enabled on the deal, you will be able to allocate a Looksee to the deal without getting stopped
### Allocation Managers should no longer get this type of error:
- New Step Logic for Begin Workflow: Allocation vs. Steps
- At Begin Workflow, if iManage finds there are more roles allocated than there are the related steps (or vice versa), the step will fail o Note: If a deal is temp-allocated, the check will be enforced.  For example, if the workflow has the Looksee – Signoff step enabled and a shelf-allocated deal temporarily gets allocated, it will need to have a temp Looksee assigned
- Temp Allocation Bug

- As above, if there is an additional delivery in the middle of the workflow that was completed and you Revert To that step (or prior), the Selective Delivery form will pop so you can tell the system whether or not you want that additional delivery to be done again

- Post Deliverables Step (WorkflowStepID 22)

- A Pre-Condition can be setup on the step to not begin until a certain date/time each period

- If the deal has the Fund Accounting service enabled, the step will export any files setup in the Export Text section of the Export tab
- Ex. After the Deliver Final Reports step is completed, an updated loan pricing file is received.  Can import the file and, if enabled, the Loan Accounting Report will automatically be exported and emailed to the party setup in the Files setup.

- Once the Deliver Final Reports step is completed successfully, the deal will move down to the Completed section

- The Automation tab will still be active, but the Revert To buttons will be disabled for all prior steps
- Once the step is completed, the deal will be marked with a green box to indicate that it is done
- If the step needs to be re-run, the Revert To button will be active for that step only
- If any of the prior steps need to be rerun, the deal will need to be Revised
- Workflow Reset – Exception
- You may recall that certain actions will reset active workflows, such as when workflow setup is changed
- If Post Deliverables is the only outstanding step and the deal has already been delivered, any such actions will not reset the workflow and will only be implemented on future workflows
- If workflow is on this step, importing into specific Fund Accounting tables is allowed without having to reset workflows

- Add Timeouts for Macros - iManage and iTax
- For both iManage and iTax, a time threshold has been set for every macro
- If automation processing of any macro exceeds the timeout threshold, automation will fail the macro and kill the Excel process that was running it so the file gets released
- Tip: Macros may time out during busy processing times, but you should be able to retry within a few minutes without running into a locked file situation
- If retrying fails, o Try running the macro manually to see if it runs longs and if so, work with your manager to troubleshoot issues with the actual file o When opening the file, check to see if there is a sensitivity label assigned to it.  If so, refer
- o
- to Unknown Password / Sensitivity Label (Web view)

- Additional Macro Processing Enhancements
- One or more errors occurred (0x800AC472) o This error randomly happens when a macro request doesn’t even go through o If this error occurs, system will now kill the related Excel process so that the file does not stay locked/open and user can retry the step
- Conflicting step vs. macro status o Sometimes we would get mixed messages on the UI, such as when the macros show as successful, but the step shows that a macro had failed
- This happened because the actual macros ran successfully, but the system failed to close the file correctly
- The logic was updated to only mark the macros as successful if the system was able to close the file correctly

- Setup

- The validation will not be added to the step automatically when setting up a Global Duty for automation for the first time o You must manually enable the validation if you want it to be run
- Backup Servicing Workflow Enhancement
- The Backup Servicing template now includes a “Check Report – Processor” step that users can enable within their workflow, if desired
- When enabling the step, you will be notified that the related task has not been setup yet
- You must go to the Ongoing Tasks tab to setup the file that you want to be checked on that step o Select Backup Servicing from the dropdown o Hit Add Universal Tasks o In the File Location form that pops, populate the File Location.  Filemasks can be used.  U: drive files can also be setup.
- Once saved, the task should appear on the main grid
- File Deliverables Enhancements
- File Date Check
- At Deliver Final Reports, we currently do a check so that if the Final Package has a modified date/time greater than the Reviewer Signoff date/time, the signoff will fail • We have now expanded that so that the check can be done at any workflow step, for any file
- In Deal Setup > Files, a new field was added that allows you to select which step you want to compare the modify date/time to - "Date Check".
- On the step when the file is delivered, the system will compare the file's current modify date/time to the “Date Check” step's signoff (EndDate).  If file’s date/time is greater than the specified step's signoff, it will fail.
- If no WF step is setup for the file, the check will happen on the Deliver Final Reports step, by default
- For example, suppose the Rate Reset Report is usually finalized at Signoff -Processor and delivered at Deliver Final Reports.
- The file would be setup with a Date Check of “Signoff – Processor”
- Suppose Signoff – Processor is completed on 3/6/2024 @ 7 p.m.
- At Deliver Final Reports, the system will check the modify date/time of the _8 file
- If the file’s date/time is less than 7 p.m., it will deliver the file
- If the file’s date/time is greater than the Signoff – Processor date/time, it will fail because the file was changed after it had been approved
- This new feature can be combined with additional file deliveries for any step during the workflow.
- For example, suppose the Rate Reset Report needs to be emailed at the Signoff – Reviewer step and delivered at Deliver Final Reports.
- Suppose Signoff – Processor is completed on 3/6/2024 @ 8:06 p.m.
- At Signoff - Reviewer, the system will check the modify date/time of the _8 file o If the file’s date/time is less than 8:06 p.m., the file had not been changed and the file will be emailed out
- If the file’s date/time is greater than the Signoff – Processor date/time, it will fail because the file was changed after it had been approved
- Processing
- Hide Lock Deal Button

- If you run into a scenario where you need to “lock” a deal, please reach out to Linda Mai immediately
- Post Macro-Import Process - Mismatch Balance File Not Exported
- When importing files with the old SSIS maps via iManage, there is a post-import process that runs any sprocs attached to the map o iManage would execute the sproc(s) immediately after a successful import of that map
- Since most maps have now converted to SQL maps and files are imported using LoadiMap_IR, the Import Engine has been updated to similarly run associated sprocs after maps are loaded via the macro
- If the map is tied to any sprocs in tblSpListMap, once the SQL map is successfully imported, the sprocs will be run
- For example, map 2061, which is the SQL version of map 1619 is associated with these 3 sprocs
- o If using either LoadiMap_IR or iManage to import the property file using map 2061, if the import is successful, these 3 sprocs will automatically be run
- ▪ If there is a mismatch between the balances in the property file vs. the periodic file, the _MisMatchBalRows_ will be exported to the deal’s T: folder
- If there are other SQL maps that need to have sprocs run post-import, please submit an iTracker to get them added to the table

### The bug has been fixed for non-automated deals:
- Automation Self-Start Bugs
- Terminated Deals
- There was an instance when a user accidentally loaded a file for a terminated deal and that kicked off the new period’s workflow
- The logic has been fixed to not kick off workflow for any periods post-termination to eliminate erroneous records
- Self-Start: FileID with Deal Date Code
- Automation self-start should only occur if all of the enabled features below are met for the period o FileIDs - once all Required and Optional (Expected) are loaded o Deal level date/time setup o Child/Parent dependences
- However, workflow would get initiated once all FileIDs are loaded even if deal level date code/time had not been met o Now, workflow will wait until the deal date/time has been met until kicking off (as long as all FileIDs have been loaded and parent deals are done, if setup)
### Example: even though this deal’s FileID was loaded, the workflow didn’t automatically kick off until the deal’s date/time had been met on the 7th:
- Allocations
- Step Check Enhancement
- Previously, we did a generic step check on the Allocations screen – if there were any outstanding/active workflows, a change in allocations would reset all those workflows o Ex. if you reassigned deals for a future month, the current signoffs blew out
- The check done on the Allocations screen was enhanced to take into account the EffectiveDt o Now, workflows will only reset if there are any outstanding workflows on or after the EffectiveDt
- Ex. If the February workflow is in progress, making an allocation change effective for March will no longer reset the February workflow.  If the March workflow was in progress, it would be reset.
- Shelf
- Shelf Members Unable to Lock Deals Within Shelf
### Shelf Processors should be able to do anything for shelf-allocated deals that a regular Processor can do on a hard/temp-assigned deal.  o However, there was a bug that denied shelf Processors from locking shelf-allocated deals:
- o The above error should only occur on hard/temp-allocated deals when a non-associated user tries to lock the deal.
- Now, any shelf user should be able to lock their shelf-allocated deals
### However, if you are not a part of the shelf team, you will be denied:
- Approval / Workflow
- New Mandatory Pre-Validation or Step Logic for Begin Workflow
- If an additional file deliverable (email/copy file) is setup on an automated deal, but the workflow step at which the delivery should happen was not selected, the Begin Workflow step will fail to give you the opportunity to update the setup
- The rule is that any additional file deliverables must be associated with a workflow step
- It is possible that a legacy deal already had a file setup to be emailed and then months later, the deal is automated.  If deal team doesn’t remember to tie the delivery to a step, the email will not be done.
- PDF Viewer Build Folders
- The PDF Viewer application that is used to open files for review during the Check Report – Processor/Reviewer steps have been integrated into the iManage build to help with performance
- The hope is that now that the application is housed on each user’s machine (along with iManage) as opposed to being housed on a shared drive, the constant freezing of the step will be eliminated
- Ready for Review Email Language
- For automated deals, the Ready for Review email notifications that go out to opted-in users after
- Processor Signoff was completed was stating the wrong user's name in the email body
### (Reviewer’s name instead of Processor’s name) o The emails have now been fixed to reflect the correct (user who ran the step or initiated the workflow) name:
- Signoff Logic Updates for No Active Loans
- As mentioned previously, we will be removing the Lock button in Data-Actions > Process > Export tab soon
- One common reason analysts were using the button were for deals that had no active loans for the period
- At Signoff – Processor, the step would fail because iServ data had not been finalized and they would “lock” the deal to trick iManage to think that collateral data had been processed, even if there were none to process
- Now, during the Process Data step, if there are no loans for the period, it will set the status to “Finalized”
- Then at the Signoff – Reviewer step, if a Loan Level file needed to be created, it would fail due to no loan data for the period
### Now, the Loan Level file will still generate even if there is no data – file would generate with just headers:
- Note!: with these exceptions in place, please take special care in ensuring that deals that do have collateral data to process are actually processed and Loan Level files are populated as expected
- Step Check Exception Still Require Unlock?
- As previously mentioned, some deals require supplemental data to be loaded that does not affect collateral or payment calculations, such as Special Servicing or Breach comments
- Exceptions were put in place for specific tables that allowed for the import of supplemental comments without unnecessary stops
- However, users were still getting the following error when trying to load into
- 'vwAgencyBreachReview', even when the workflow was at or before the Reprocess Supplemental Reports workflow step
- Now, users should not need to unlock the deal to load to an exception table as long as their workflow is at or before the Reprocess Supplemental Reports workflow step
### If users try to import these files after the Reprocess Supplemental Reports workflow step, they will be warned that continuing will reset the workflow:
- Hitting Yes will reset the workflow back to the Reprocess Supplemental Reports workflow step and load the file, without the need to unlock
- Send/Deliver Final Reports Business Logic
- The business logic of the Deliver Final Reports step includes posting files to Pivot o However, it was not discerning between files with or without a TIR code
- Now, if there are any additional file deliverables setup on the Deliver Final Reports step (to email or copy to another location), iManage will only attempt to post the file if it has a TIR code associated with it
- If there is no TIR code, it will simply email/copy the file
### There was another bug that prevented the file to be emailed if setup to do so – that has also been fixed:
- The process was also updated to skip deleted/disabled files and to account for folder/file name casing differences
- Send/Deliver Logic Changes for MTM
- Previously, if a file was setup for "Send ONLY on MTM", iManage would incorrectly try to deliver the file even in a non-MTM
- Now, when delivering at any step, iManage will check the MTM flag to see if it should be delivered for that period or not o For non-automated deals, it will sweep the file to Pivot at the Send (legacy) step based on the MTM flag
- If email or copy to new location is setup for the file,
- If a workflow step is setup for that file, it will email/copy on the step based on MTM selection
- For non-automated deals, it will email/copy at Send (legacy) based on MTM selection
- If MTM selection is not specified in the file deliverable setup, it will send the file every period by default
- In the MTM, if the file is setup to be emailed/copied, the file will be reflected in the FileCount column of the Automation tab on the related workflow step
- Reminder: the FileCount only reflects additional file deliverables (email/copy)
- Permission the Zap/Add button to Senior Managers only
- Now that the tax team has an alternative method to load tax related items, the Zap/Add buttons in the My Deals > Payments screen will be locked down after a deal is completed o Only Senior Managers will be able to zap or add on a delivered deal
- Enable My Deals Section for Collateral Deals
- For automated deals, most of the features in the My Deals > Processing screen are disabled intentionally
- However, the "View Delivered Report By Selected Month" was disabled for Collateral deals incorrectly and has now been made available
- Revision for Non-Bond Deals Bugs
- The Revise button in the My Deals > Processing screen will now be available for all automated deals, once they are complete for the selected period
- Although the idea of revision doesn't really exist for Backup Servicing, Fund Accounting and Global Duty deals, there are times when business needs to redo the process even after the deal is complete so the Revise button will now be enabled for them
### For all non-Bond deals, the result should be as follows:
### No need to fill out the Revision form o If answer yes to the pop-up, system will:
- Archive tblCompleted into tblCompleted_History for the DID/Dt
- Insert record into tblRevisionHistory with EvID 156 "I-Revised-Distrib Error [Formulas / Waterfall Issues (Excluding Input)]"
- Reset workflow back to Begin Workflow
### Note: If the non-Bond deal does not have a separate user assigned as the Reviewer, you will be denied:
- Revision logic for bond deals will remain the same, i.e. must complete the Revision form, workflow resets based on EvID, etc.
- Tax Processing
- Quarterly Delivery
- For quarterly files that need to be emailed to holders, if the tax deal folder’s name didn’t match the DID due to case differences, the email would fail
- The email API has been updated to account for the case difference and should no longer fail or require folder name to be changed
- Version 7.0.2.9 (Release Date: 2/7/2024)
- Wednesday, February 7, 2024	8:42 PM
- Automated Emails
- Recent bank policy prevented emails to be sent automatically from iManage
- Going forward, all emails that used to be generated by iManage will be sent via APIs.  From an end-user standpoint, you should not notice any difference between how the emails used to look and how they do now.
### Automated emails include:
- SSIS import fails o Large Wire
- Ready for Review - If Reviewer/Looksee is opted into emails, they will be notified once Processor/Reviewer Signoff is completed o Preliminary File Delivery: Once Reviewer Signoff step is complete, sent to Cash Analyst
- File Delivery: Once Send/Deliver Final Report step is complete, sent to Account Admin and Cash Analyst o Additional file delivery via email – as setup in Deal Setup > Files o Retractions – revision notice sent to Account Admin and Cash Analyst and RESEC deal teams o Terminations - sent to Account Admin and Cash Analyst o Insurance claims – sent to Account Admin
- Note: Please notify Linda Mai if any emails are still not being sent or if there is something wrong with the emails that are sent.
- Setup
- New Workflow for Global Duty
- A new workflow specific for Global Duty deals has been created
- This new workflow will only be available to deals that has Global Duty enabled
- The workflow will only have the basic signoff steps and no mandatory validations
- As with any other workflow template, you can set up Pre-Conditions, Pre-Validations, Macros, Post-Validations, and Check Points at any step
- Remove Mandatory Validations from Backup Servicing Steps
- All mandatory validations have been removed from the Backup Servicing template
- The validations available to be enabled no longer include validations that are related to Bond processing
- Hide SupportPackage_IR From Macro Options
- The "SupportPackage_IR" macro has been removed from the options in the Deal Setup > Processing >Workflow > Macros tab for each workflow step.
- o If enabled, it conflicts with the Support Package logic in automation
- The macro is still available for legacy deals
- MTM Validation at Check Point Setup
- • If MTM is flagged in the CheckPoint – Step Setup form, but MTM is not setup in Deal Setup, the update will fail to remind you to first setup MTM
- Allocations
- Reinstate Allocations (Setup) Check
- In the Allocations screen, when users hit the Update button, iManage will check if the deal is automated and compare the requested allocations to the deal’s enabled workflow steps
- Basically, allocations and workflow signoff steps (Processor, Reviewer and Looksee) must always be in sync
- If you want to unallocate a role, you must first disable the related step in the workflow
- The deal(s) and details of the fail will automatically be copied to your Office clipboard. You can immediately paste the details to Notepad to troubleshoot.
### The update will fail if the selected deal(s):
- Doesn't have the related signoff step enabled o Still has the workflow step enabled for the role you are trying to unassign
- Shelf Allocations
- Due to the above changes, in order to allocate a deal to a shelf, you must now modify both the Processor and Reviewer to “Not Avail.” o The simultaneous update of both roles will trigger shelf-allocation
- As a reminder, deals can only be shelf-allocated if: o The deal is assigned to a valid shelf – not blank and not the None_shelf o The deal’s shelf has members assigned to it o All of the deal’s Initial Tasks have been completed
- File Deliverables Enhancements
- The following stories are related to additional file deliverables that are setup via Deal Setup > Files tab for email and/or file copy to a different location during workflow steps.  They are NOT related to file posting to Pivot done at the Deliver Final Report step.
- Additional Email Options Not Working
- • There was a bug that prevented the “Send Email From Processor” and “cc:” to work correctly in the email delivery of files, but should be fixed now
- File Deliverables: MTM Validation
- • A check has been added in the case when MTM is not setup on a deal, but you choose to setup a file delivery based on MTM
- File Deliverables: Investor Files Tab
- • Whenever an additional file deliverable is completed at any given workflow step, the details (when and who) of that delivery will also be recorded in the My Deals > Investor Files tab
- Add Override Fail Option to Files Tab
- • If an additional file delivery fails, you now have the option to override the fail so the step can be marked as successful and workflow can continue
- FileID Enhancements
- The following stories are related to FileIDs setup in Data-Actions > Setup > Servicer Setup > Import File Setup screen.
- Add Step Check at FileID Setup
### If you try to make the following changes to a FileID while the deal’s workflow is running, you will be reminded that you must stop the workflow in order to make any setup changes:
### If you try to make FileID setup changes on a deal that has an outstanding workflow (not in progress, but also not complete yet), you will get a warning that your signoffs will be wiped out if you continue with the setup change:
- If you confirm to continue, the outstanding workflow will revert back to the Process Data step
- FileID Setup - Unable to Delete Date Code
- Previously, if a Date Code was setup on a FileID, there wasn’t a way to remove the code.
### A Delete button has been added to the Checkpoint – File Setup form:
- MTM-FileID Logic
- The MTM checkbox is now working and can be used to tie a FileID to the deal level MTM (in Deal Setup)
- If the MTM checkbox is flagged, but MTM is not setup in Deal Setup, upon the Insert or Update/Save button, it will fail and remind you to setup MTM first
- Example: A deal has 5 FileIDs and on the deal level, MTM is setup as January.  4 for the FileIDs are not flagged for MTM which means they should be checked for every month.  1 FileID is flagged for MTM which means automation will only check for the file in January.
### o In January, if the MTM FileID is:
- ▪ Required or Optional (Expected) – workflow will not automatically kickoff until the FileID is loaded
- If Optional (Expected) FileID is not loaded, user can still manually kick off the workflow
- ▪ Optional (Not Expected) – workflow will kick off even if the FileID is not loaded o For every other month, automation will not even consider the MTM FileID and will automatically kickoff as soon as the other Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs are loaded
- Daily Overdue FileIDs Report
- • The Daily Overdue FileIDs email notification was fixed to make the report name consistent and to exclude deals that are already complete for the period
- Automation Self-Start: Resec
- Self-Start: One Child, Multiple Parents
- You can now setup a deal’s workflow to start once all of its underlying are done with their workflows (or a specific step) o This only works if all the underlying deals are internal, automated deals
- Child’s deal processing method must be set to Cloud Automation and workflow has never been initiated before for that given period
- Setup can be done through the DMT under iManage > tblWFUnderlyingDealSetup
### Tips for setup:
- For UnderlyingDealSetupID (red column) – use 0 for each row
- Populate the TpIDs, WorkflowStep, and Shelf fields – for better management tracking o In the example above, Resec TPMT 2021-R1’s workflow will automatically kick-off once its 6 underlying deals’ workflows are completed
- Note: There is a bug where if a deal has a FileID setup, automation is not considering if a deal date code has also been setup before kicking off the workflo, i.e. as soon as all required FileIDs are loaded, workflow kicks off even if deal’s date code has not been yet.  This bug will be fixed with the next release.
- Processing
- Hardcoded Maps – CSV/Text Imports
- Hardcoded maps that import csv/txt files should now load without issue
- Ex. Map 2, 870, 874, 1063, 1120, 1392, etc.
- Add ProcessingStatus to Deleted Data Grid
- • If an import fails, the reason for the fail will now be displayed in the ProcessingStatus field of the Data-Actions > Processing > Import tab > Import Log (Deleted) grid • The message can be copied and pasted for easier reading
- Missing Loans on Resec
- If there were missing CUSIPs for a Resec deal, iManage was failing to export the Mismatched Loans file
- That bug has been fixed.  Now, at Process, if there are missing CUSIPs, iManage will correctly trigger the missing loans notification on the UI and export the corresponding Mismatched Loans files to the deal’s T: drive folder
- Add Note to the Lock Deal Button
- In Data-Actions > Processing > Export tab, we’ve added a notice that the Lock Deal button will be removed after 3/31/2023
- If you are regularly using the button in order to get through automation, please reach out to Linda Mai with details (deals, periods, etc.) so your scenario can be handled via code
- Approval / Workflow
- Display WorkflowStepID Instead of Seq in Automation Tab
- • To provide an easy reference for the StepID of each workflow step for setting up child/parent relationships in tblWFUnderlyingDealSetup, the My Deals > Automation tab now displays the Step ID instead of the SEQ number
- Quotation & Times in Loan Level File
- • System generated Loan Level files should no longer generate with quotation marks or times in the date columns
- Post Validation Override Bug
- If a post validation fails on any step, status updates that are usually done by that step will be reverted back
- If the failed post validation is overridden, the system was not re-updating the status (such as processing status or tblCompleted) accordingly
### Automation logic has been updated so that:
- o If a failed post-validation is overridden for the Process Data workflow step, the deal’s ProcessStatus will be updated to "Processed" o If a failed post-validation is overridden for the Accept Data workflow step, the deal’s ProcessStatus will be updated to "Finalized" o If a failed post-validation is overridden for the Processor Signoff workflow step, tblCompleted will be updated to reflect the signoff ▪ Same with Reviewer and Looksee signoffs
- Failed U: Drive Access
- Previously, automation was not able to access the U: drive correctly, except for macro processing.
- File validations and additional file delivery (email or copy to new location) of a file that resides on the U: drive would fail.
- Access to the U: drive for automation has been fixed so these features should work correctly now.  Please notify Linda Mai if they don’t.
- New Late Reasons – Automation-Related
### Automation-related reasons have been added as options to the Late Reason form:
- File Deliverables File Count and Files Tab Enhancement
- The Files tab in the Step Reports will only include additional file deliverables that are setup to be copied to a new folder or to be emailed o It no longer includes any legacy file deliverables - those will stay tracked in the Investor Files tab
- Count in the Automation grid will reflect the same as the Files tab o Ex. If no files are to be copied/emailed at the Deliver Final Reports step, the File Count will report as 0 and the Files tab will list nothing for that step
- Update Going Green Logic for First Period
- When running the Check Report workflow steps for the first period, it would always throw an error that the prior period’s package could not be found o If it’s the first period, there would obviously not be a prior package so the message was unnecessary and confusing
- The logic for the steps has been updated to no longer try to find the prior package during the first period, i.e. no more failed message
- Selective File Delivery Form Popping Unnecessarily
- • For additional file deliveries, the Selective File Delivery form should only pop if a file had already been delivered.  However, it was popping when reverting a workflow even when the file had never been delivered before.
- o Ex. There are 3 files setup to be emailed at Deliver Final Reports, but Prepare Distrib fails during workflow.  When rerunning the Prepare Distrib step, the form should not pop since the file was never emailed before.
- Due Date Logic Update
- The due date listed in various places in the My Deals screen were not always the same, which can cause a deal to be late
### The logic for the due date calculation is now consistent in all places on the screen:
- Deal list under Bond or Show All views (Incomplete or Complete panels) o In the Report Schedule > Due Date field
### One exception is if checkpoints are setup on any workflow step o Example: Without any checkpoints, this deal’s due date is 2/16:
- If checkpoints are setup at various steps of the workflow…
- The Due Date listed in the Report Schedule will reflect the earliest checkpoint for quick reference
- ▪ Note: The due date in the Incomplete panel will always display the deal’s true due date
- ReviewDiscrepancies File Not Exported
- Due to a deal folder name case sensitivity issue, the Reviewer Signoff workflow step was failing to find the correct folder to export the ReviewDiscrepancies file to
- That bug has been fixed as the API will now be able to locate the deal folder even if the casing doesn’t match what is listed in Deal Setup
- Capture Who Skipped Macro
- • Since it is possible for a user to skip macros ahead of time, we are now capturing who skips macros in tblWorkflowMacroProcessPeriodic (for management tracking)
- Regenerate Cover Page at Package Reports for Terminations
## As stated in the prior release notes, if a deal is terminating and uses one of the below Table of Contacts pages, the Next Payment will generate as N/A
- Agency o AgencyWLS
- CMSA
- RMBS Flex
- Note: How the page generates will depend on whether or not the termination date is populated at the time of the Auto Reports o For example, if you know a deal is terminating prior to the workflow, you can populate the date in Deal Setup (just prior to running Auto Reports) and when manually Auto Reporting or running the Generate Auto Reports step, it will generate the N/A so that when the deal gets to the Package Report step, the package should be correct
- However, if you don't know that it is terminating and just go through the workflow, you will notice the Termination Form pops at the Package Report step (when it notices that the bonds pay down to
- 0).
- ▪ (Enhancement) If you confirm the deal is truly terminating, the workflow will automatically revert to the Auto Reports step so that it regenerates the cover page as desired and then redo the workflow so that the package includes the new cover page.
- After hitting Continue, you will be notified that the workflow is reverting back, i.e. you no longer have to remember to manually revert the workflow
- Upon Refresh, you will see that workflow had reverted back to generate “N/A” on the cover page for the next payment date
- Signoff Fails When No Internal Admin
- For deals with insurance claims, we normally require that an internal Account Administrator is setup on the deal so that claims can be emailed to the AA
### However, for deals that don’t have internal AAs, workflow would fail:
- For these deals, please enable the Skip Email Notifications in Deal Setup > Other Settings as the Processor Signoff step has been updated to skip the AA check if the setting is turned on
- IREM Enhancements
- Date Filter Default
- Starting a couple a few months ago, the Date filter (on top) defaulted to "Select", which required users to find the current period manually
### The Date filter has been fixed to default to the current month when you first load the IREM:
### The dropdown lists the more current periods on top for easier navigation:
- New “Not Started” Status
- Previously, many deals were listed on the IREM with a blank Current Step and Step Status and it was unclear what was happening with them
### IREM has been updated to handle the different scenarios:
- For automated deals whose workflows haven’t started yet, the Step Status will now show as “Not Started”
- Non-monthly deals that don’t pay in the selected period will no longer appear in that period’s deal list
- ▪ Ex. NFL Sr 2018-2024 is a semi-annual deal that pays in April and October only.  For all other periods, it will not appear in the result set.
- The Step Status column will now be ordered (by default) as follows: o Failed o Stopped o Cancelled o Not Started o Initiated o In Progress o Delivered
- The top filters have also been updated.
- The Sort By filter now includes an option to sort by Current Step that will display deals that have “Not Started” on top
- The Step Status filter also includes “Not Started”
- Version 7.0.2.8 (Release Date: 12/7/2023)
- Thursday, December 7, 2023	7:47 PM
- Setup
- Enhance Payment Date with Prior Month Logic *
- In Deal Setup > Basic Info > Dates tab, there is a new checkbox for Prior Month in the Distribution Date section o This can be used when payment date logic is like 17 business days after the 15th of the month
- Previously, custom payment dates had to be setup to handle this type of logic, but it is common enough that we’ve updated iManage to handle it correctly o Note: If you have any custom payment dates setup on these deals, they will need to be deleted in order for the new calculation to work correctly
- Once enabled, the My Deals screen will correctly display the deal in the period that there is a payment date
- Ex. the above quarterly deal will show up in Aug, Nov, Feb, and May with the correct payment/due dates and not in July, Oct, Jan or April
- Month(s) That Matter aka MTM
- In Deal Setup > Main Info tab, there is a new section for MTM where you can identify significant months for a deal
- For example, if your monthly deal has additional requirements every quarter (Jan, Apr, July, Oct), you could flag those months in this section and refer to those special months in the features described below
- If this MTM section is left unflagged, all features will consider the action needs to be done every period by default
- Automation Workflow Template Setup
- • For users who assign workflow templates to deals for first time automation, please be aware that you must now select the Service Type and then you can select the Template.
- o With the addition of the Backup Servicing template (more details below), the order is now 1) Service Type, then 2) Templates
- File Deliverables Enhancements
- New File Types
### New file types have been added to the File Type dropdown:
- o “Verification Letter”
- Ex. can be used for Backup Servicing deals o “Preliminary Report”
- Ex. Can be used for preliminary client approval
- These File Types do not have TIR codes so will not post to Pivot
- Allow for Filemasks
- Both the File Location and New Folder fields were updated to allow for file masks, such as {DID} or {yyyy}
- WF Step Setup
- If you would like any of the files to be copied to a shared drive (J:, M:, T: or U:) or emailed at any point in the workflow, you can set them up via the WF Step dropdown
- Select the workflow step you want and enable at least one of the additional delivery features – New Folder or Send Email o The delivery will NOT include sweeping to Pivot.  That will still only happen at the Deliver Final Reports workflow step.
- Ex. The Preliminary Report can be setup to be emailed at the Signoff – Reviewer  step to get request client approval o Note: Since these additional file deliveries will be tracked separately from the Pivot file deliveries, please do NOT setup the Distribution Report (TIR code 203) for this scenario and use the Preliminary Report file type instead.
- Automation Tab – FileCount and Files Tab
### In the Automation tab, the grid will now display the number of files that are setup for delivery at each step:
- o The FileCount for the Deliver Final Reports step will include all active files that have been historically been sent at this step
- Step Report – Files Tab
- The Step Report now includes a tab named “Files” with the details of the file that was setup for the additional delivery
- For example, if the Preliminary Report was setup to be emailed as part of the Signoff – Reviewer step, the file will be emailed as desired and the Files tab will show Email Sent = Yes
### Note: If a file deliverable fails during the workflow step, the step will also be considered a fail:
- Selective Delivery Form
- After revising a deal or if reverting/resetting a workflow, since the files had already been delivered during the original signoffs, you will get a Selective Delivery pop-up asking you if you want to redeliver the report
- o In this example, it’s asking do we want to re-email the Distribution Report to the client for approval at Reviewer Signoff
- Hit Send Files if you want to resend
- Hit Cancel to not resend
- If the "Selective Report Delivery" setting is enabled on the deal and files setup to be delivered on various steps, the Selective Delivery form will pop twice at Begin Workflow o 1) Normal delivery files done at Deliver Final Reports step
### 2) Then pop-up for the additional delivery:
- MTM (Months That Matter)
- By default, the file will be delivered every month.  However, if you want certain files to only be sent by email or copied to a shared folder in special months, you can change the MTM selection to match your preference
- As long as MTM is set for your deal in the Main Info tab, you can select: o Send ONLY on MTM to only email/copy the file in the indicated months o Or Do NOT send on MTM to email/copy the file in all the other months
- Revert Workflow If Update File Setup
- • If your deal has a workflow in progress and you make any changes to Deal Setup > Files (Add/Modify/Delete), your workflow will be reset to Begin Workflow
- Additional Email Options *
- If you want your file to be emailed, but showing the email as from the Processor, simply flag the Processor checkbox
- You can also CC and BCC your email to other recipients in the new fields
- Example, for this deal, Jason Kocsis is the processor so even if the file is sent during the Reviewer steps, the email will show coming from Jason
- Workflow Step Checkpoint
- Automation Workflow Template Setup
- If your deal requires certain things to be done during the month, prior to the Deliver Final Reports step, you can setup Checkpoints for any of the workflow steps
- In Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow, there is a new column called Check Point
- Click on the button to the right of the cell for the step you want to setup a checkpoint
- The Checkpoint form will open that is similar to the Pre-Condition form – Date Code must be populated.  If all other fields are left blank, they will default to NYC for Country fields and 12:00 a.m. CST.
- In this example, I setup a weekly checkpoint at 10 a.m. CST – one for each workflow step
- There is an option to set the Checkpoint only for MTM o Ex. If you need to do something prior to Deliver Final Reports, but only for certain months, you could set the applicable MTM in the Main Info tab and then set a Checkpoint at the Signoff – Processor step with MTM flagged
- o Then that Checkpoint would apply in the MTM
- If you want the new checkpoints to be applied to a period that already has a workflow going, please make sure you hit the main Save button in the workflow template setup screen
- •
- •
- Automation Grid - Checkpoints
- • The My Deals > Automation tab will display the Checkpoints that you set
- Due Date Displayed
- In the My Deals > Processing tab, the Due Date will display the earlier of the deal’s Due Date or the earliest unresolved checkpoint so you can know ahead of time that something is coming up due o That means the Due Date displayed may change as the month progresses if there are multiple checkpoints
- In this example, the deal is due on the 22nd, but because there is a checkpoint for the 20th, the Due Date will show the 20th
- If one of the checkpoints were flagged for MTM and the period is not one of the MTM, the checkpoint will not appear in the Automation tab for that period
- Automation Self Start
- Previously, a workflow would only kick off once all of a deal’s FileIDs are loaded
### Workflows can now be configured to automatically start based on any combination of:
- FileIDs - once all Required and Optional (Expected) are loaded o Deal level date/time setup
- Child/Parent workflow step executed relationship (different deals) o Child/Parent relationship (same deal, different service type, i.e. tax) o Child/Shelf relationship
- Now, if any of these are setup on a deal, those items must be met before the workflow will kick off automatically
### Self-Start will only work if:
- Child deal is in Cloud Automation mode
- Workflow for period has never been initiated for the Child deal o All Child/Parent/Shelf deals are automated
- Enhancements to FileIDs
- The Data-Actions > Setup > Servicer Setup > Import File Setup section has been enhanced with new optional fields.
- Note: Workflows will continue to automatically kick off once all Required and Optional_Expected FileIDs are loaded.
- Note: The Edit/Save button is now all the way to the right of the grid – scroll to the right to access the button.
- FileID Setup: Map 0 for Non-Imported Files
- We are often required to confirm we received a certain file, but not actually have to import it, such as part of our backup servicing duties. A FileID can now be setup for this scenario so there is a historical record saved in our database.
- When setting up a FileID that does not need to be imported, the File Type and File Name must be populated and the Map must be set to 0
### In the Process > Import tab, the FileID will appear and once you receive and saved the file to the necessary folder, you would hit Load and navigate to the saved file to record that the file was received and where it is saved o In this example, assume I received the file via email and saved it in the deal’s M: monthly data folder.  Upon Load, I would navigate to that file:
- o The Loaded Data grid (tblImportLog) now has a record of the FileID being completed with the exact path of where the file is saved
- You can “Delete” these FileIDs and “Re-load” them as needed
- Note: Keep in mind that if you have multiple FileIDs setup with Map = 0, the Loaded Data grid will not show which record goes with which FileID
- FileID Setup: MTM
- You may notice a MTM column in the Import File Setup feature, but please disregard it
- In a future release, you will be able to tie a FileID to the above-mentioned deal level MTM.  More details to come at that time.
- FileID Setup: Date Code/Time
- If there is a file that you expect to get by a certain date/time and want a reminder that the file has not yet been received/imported, you can setup a Date Code for that FileID
- For example, suppose you expect to get the Comments file two business days prior to payment date.  Hit Add in the Date Code column for the file and a “Checkpoint – File Setup form” will open where you can setup a date code (with time and Country Code adjustments) o If Country fields and Time are not populated, they will default to NYC and 12:00 AM CST, respectively
- If the date has passed without the FileID being “loaded”, you will receive an email notification starting the morning after with the details of the FileID to remind you to follow-up on the file
- FileID Setup: Destination Folder
- Suppose you can receive a file in various ways, but you always need to save a copy in a specific folder.  In this case, you would setup your FileID with the Destination Folder populated.
- If a file name is not populated in the file mask for the Destination Folder, the file will be copied with the same file name as your source file
- Upon Load, navigate to your source file and it will be copied to the Destination Folder
- If your source file name is known, you can also setup your FileID with a File Default Location
- Upon Load, the system will check if the source file as defined in the File Default Location exists o If Destination Folder is not populated and if the source file exists, the FileID will be marked as completed (with no need to navigate to the file) o If Destination Folder is populated and the source file exists, the source file will be copied to the destination and the FileID will be marked as completed
- The Destination Folder field can be used for any FileID, including existing FileIDs that are used for importing o If a Destination Folder is setup on an imported FileID, it will first try to copy the source file to the Destination Folder
- If the copy fails, the FileID will fail, i.e. import will not be done
- Importing will only be done if the copy to the Destination Folder is successful
- Ability to Self-Start Based on a Date/Time
- In the Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab, there is a new Workflow DateCode feature
- If you want your deal’s workflow to automatically start on a certain day/time every period, click on Add Datecode.
- o The Date Code must be populated
- ▪ If you hover over the DateCode Legend, the legend will appear to help you formulate your Date Code o The Time is based on Central standard time o Similar to the Pre-Condition form, you have the options to populate the Country Code, Country Code Adj and Time fields.  If you don’t, they will default to NYC, NYC, and 12:00 a.m. (CST), respectively.
- Suppose your deal doesn’t have any FileIDs, you can use this new Date/Time setup to kick off the workflow on the date that you set instead.  Or if you don’t want your workflow to start until a certain date/time, even if all the FileIDs have been loaded, you can set the Workflow DateCode for that.
- Once it hits the designated Workflow DateCode/Time, it will automatically kick off the workflow o Note: the job runs every 5 minutes so it could be delayed by up to 5 minutes
### Ex. Above deal’s workflow automatically kicked off within a couple of minutes of the set time:
- Ability to Self-Start Based on Another Deal
- There is now an option to setup a deal’s workflow to start as soon as another deal is done with any action within its workflow o For example, you can setup a NIM to kick off as soon as the parent deal’s workflow is done (or as soon as the parent’s Reviewer Signoff step is done)
- For those with access to DMT, you may set this up via tblWFUnderlyingDealSetup
- o In the above example, SMT1997-1 is setup to kick off as soon as SH 2019-SBA1 completes Processor Signoff (WorkflowStep 10) o If WorkflowStep is left blank, the ChildDID’s workflow will kick off as soon as the ParentDID’s entire workflow is complete o If TpID fields are left blank, they will default to 1 for Bond
- Ability to Self-Start Based on a Shelf
- There is also an option to setup a deal’s workflow to start once all the deals in a shelf are done with their workflows or a specific step,i.e. for a Global Duty o Example: There is a deal that is dependent on all the deals within the Velocity_shelf being done.  Similar to above, you can set the ChildDID to the dependent deal and as soon as all the Velocity deals are done, the child’s workflow will automatically kick off.
- Suppose you have a Global Duty to run something after the 25th Bayview deals are done
- o With this setup, once all automated deals in the Bayview shelf are done for the period, the workflow for GR - Post 25th Bayview will kick off automatically
- In tblWFUnderlyingDealSetup, set the shelf name as the ParentDID and set Shelf to TRUE
- Note: Self-start based on multiple parent deals, such as for Resecs, has not been implemented yet.  More details to come when that is released.
- Putting It Altogether
### As stated above, a deal’s workflow can now be configured to automatically start based on any combination of:
- o FileIDs - once all Required and Optional (Expected) are loaded o Deal level date/time setup o Child/Parent workflow step executed relationship (different deals) o Child/Shelf relationship
- Example: Deal with required FileIDs, a deal datecode of MT26BA00NA and Bayview shelf dependency will automatically kick off once all the FileIDs have been loaded, as long as it has reached the 26th of the month and once all the deals in the Bayview shelf are completed o If you want to kick off the deal’s workflow despite it still being the 25th of the month, you can still manually Begin Workflow and the workflow will run as your manual click overrides the datecode condition
- Note: There is a job that runs every 5 minutes to check that all of a deal’s self-start conditions have been met so auto kick-off might be delayed by a few minutes
- Backup Servicing Workflow
- Note: As of 12/7, our cloud services do not have access to the U: drive with access expected by mid-December.  A separate email will be sent once access is confirmed.
- New Backup Calculation Workflow Step
- A new workflow step has been created called “Backup Calculation”
- It is available as an optional workflow step that can be enabled for Bond deals for deals that have Bond and Backup duties
- The step can be setup with a pre-condition, validations and macros like any other workflow step
- New Backup Servicing Workflow
- A new workflow specific for Backup Servicing deals has been created
- If a deal has the Backup Servicing duty enabled, this new workflow will be available
- You can use the new FileID features to automatically verify file storage and file copied to U: drive prior to kicking off the workflow o At Begin Workflow, it will check if all the Required and Optional_Expected FileIDs have been “loaded”
- The workflow is comprised of the basic signoff steps.  Note: The Back Up Servicing Comment form will no longer pop at Signoff – Processor.
- o tblCompleted (My Deals > Processing tab) will get updated as you go through the workflow signoff steps
- The new “Backup Calculation” step is available as an optional step o Macros can be setup on the step to run distrib/models as needed.  Ex. Run ExportRanges_IR to export the completed verification letter (from the applicable Excel file) for the period to PDF.
### If you need to send a Verification Letter, you can set it up on one of these steps in Deal Setup > Files (once you opt into automation):
- The Deliver Final Reports step will have the Pre-Validation of Deal Team must manually validate enabled by default
- Note: The bond-related mandatory validations will be removed from the backup workflow steps in a future release.  If there are validations that you would like to create specific to backup servicing, please let us know.
- If Backup Servicing Deal Already Automated
- If you already automated your deal under a Bond workflow and it makes more sense to switch it to the Backup Servicing workflow, you will be warned that only one workflow can be setup for your deal
- Remove the Bond service from Deal Setup > Basic Info > Main Info tab o This will automatically remove the Bond allocation for the deal
- In the Allocations screen, select Backup Servicing allocation type from the dropdown and allocate your deal there • Deal will show up under the My Deals screen for Backup Servicing
- Processing
- Accept Data Enhancements
- The Accept Data logic was optimized to improve performance
- Results should be the same as before, but you should notice a faster response
- Ability to hide all account columns from the Ledger extract in Loan Accounting
- In Data-Actions > Loan Accounting > Data Extract Setup tab, there is now an option to hide the account entries from the customizable Ledger extract report. o If flagged, it will hide all of the numbered Accounts Used
- When click Export Data in the Processing Tab, the Ledger file that is exported to the T: deal folder will not include all the numbered accounts (columns H:DQ)
- Access to Loan Accounting Screen
- When navigating to Data-Actions > Loan Accounting, if the deal is not a Loan Accounting deal, it used to throw an unhandled exception error.
### Message has been updated to clarify that non-Loan Accounting deals cannot use these screens:
- Approval / Workflow
- Better Error Message When Manual Step In Progress
- If a deal seems stuck, when you hit Refresh, iManage will now tell you if the step is currently being run by someone else o Ex. Neemit is running a step so when I hit Refresh, it shows that
### Similarly, if you are able to click on the main button, but the step is actually being run by someone else, the Workflow Status form will inform you of such:
- If a Senior Manager is asked to reset a step that seems stuck, at Reset, it will notify them who is currently working on the step
- Workflow Step Completion vs. tblCompleted
- There have been various cases where the workflow seems to have failed at the Deliver Final Reports step, but deal still showed as delivered/completed in the My Deals > Processing tab
- Logic order has been adjusted so that if any of the signoff/deliver steps fail, the corresponding signoff/deliver fields in tblCompleted are also left unpopulated
- On the flip side, tblCompleted should be updated only once the corresponding signoff/deliver workflow step and all of its sub-steps are successfully completed
- Update Report Logic for Terminations
- If a deal is terminating and uses one of the below Table of Contacts pages, the Next Payment will generate as N/A o Agency
- AgencyWLS
- CMSA
- RMBS Flex
- Note: How the page generates will depend on whether or not the termination date is populated at the time of the Auto Reports o For example, if you know a deal is terminating prior to the workflow, you can populate the date in Deal Setup (just prior to running Auto Reports) and when manually Auto Reporting or running the Generate Auto Reports step, it will generate the N/A so that when the deal gets to the Package Report step, the package should be correct
- However, if you don't know that it is terminating and just go through the workflow, you will notice the Termination Form pops at the Package Report step (when it notices that the bonds pay down to 0).  If deal is truly terminating, you will need to manually run or revert to the Auto Reports step so that it regenerates the cover page as desired and then redo the workflow so that the package includes the new cover page.
- Update Locking Form for tblLockLog Records
- • The Locking form (access via My Deals > Processing > Lock button) now only displays active users in the “Pick a Verifier” dropdown options
- Check Report Not Pulling Latest Prior Report
- In a previous build, the Check Report – Processor step was updated to pull in the last modified package for the prior period into the Prior window
- However, the same update was not applied to the Check Report – Reviewer step
- Now, the Check Report - Reviewer step will also pull in the last modified package into the Prior window

- Upgraded PDF to HTML Converter
- • TOS upgraded our PDF to HTML converter so please be pay close attention to the HTML files generated by iManage
