- Automation Bug Fixes
- Step Report - Unable to Skip Macros Prior to Running Step
- Previous functionality that allowed users to skip a macro(s) prior to kicking off the step that it is enabled on stopped working.
- Bug is fixed – when workflow is at the step, users can expand the Step Report, flag the Skip checkbox in the Macros tab for the macro they want to skip and then hit Apply & Resume.  Step will start running and know to skip the flagged macro(s).
- Note: Macro for a later step cannot be skipped at the beginning of the workflow – it can only be skipped if the workflow is on the actual step.
- No Insurance Claims Emails Sent
- For insured deals, an insurance claim email should be sent at Processor Signoff if 'InsuredClaimInt' or 'InsuredClaimPrin' are found in the tax range, even if the value is 0.00.
- These email notifications were not working for automated deals but will be sent now
### If claims change, a revised claim email will be sent:
- Deliver Final Reports - Selective File Delivery Setting
- Previously, the Selective File Delivery feature (Deal Setup > Other Settings) was not working with automated deals, but should now
- As a reminder, this feature can be enabled on deals that can be delivered, despite a required file not being available yet o At Deliver Final Reports, the Selective Delivery form will open with all the files setup in Deal Setup > Files listed o Select the files that you want delivered and only those will be sent o The step will not fail if any of the unselected files are missing
- Once the required file is available, you will have to deliver the file manually via the Investor Files tab
- File Didn't Sweep
- There was an instance where the payment file did not get delivered during automation
- When delivering files, a check has been added to verify that the file(s) made it into the destination folder(s).  If not, the process will try to sweep the file one more time. o If the delivery fails a second time, the step will be marked as a fail with an explanation why
- Fix Sweep of Deals with SEC Filings
- Certain deals require SEC filing and for those deals, we sweep the final package to a special SEC Filings folder on the X: drive
- Unfortunately, we were not filtering out the SEC deals during the automation process and were creating unnecessary deal folders on the X: drive for non-SEC deals
- This bug has been fixed – for automated deals, we will only try to deliver files to the SEC folder for SEC deals
- Automation Health Check
- Extend UI Timeout to 60 Seconds
- If there are SQL database issues, it may take longer than usual for our processes to complete
- When this happens, the UI may freeze/crash even though the process is still running in the background
- To account for that, both the background code for Import, Process, Accept Data, and Auto Report and the corresponding UIs have been updated to wait a minute before timing out (and crashing)
- Notification of Failed Services
- In our ongoing effort to identify failed services before the business line is affected, TOS setup jobs that notifies them if something fails
- Most of the work done for automation is done via APIs.  Currently, there is no way for TOS to be notified at the time of the fail so business users will continue to get errors if an API, such as Auto Report, is unavailable.
- If you encounter such errors, please wait a minute before retrying the action
- APIs are setup to restart within 30 seconds (if possible)
- Therefore, if you continue to get the error after 5 minutes, please report it immediately
- TOS will be notified of the fail through a systematic check half an hour after the incident so it will be quicker of the business line reports the issue first
- Excel and Report processing is done on 10 Windows servers.  When any of those processors go down, TOS is immediately notified but there is also a job that automatically tries to restart those processors.
- If, for some reason, the auto-restart doesn’t work and the processors on all 10 servers go down, business line will get an error that a step is unable to run “due to services down.”
- If this occurs, please report the issue immediately
- Send notifications for stuck records
### Sometimes, a request can get stuck in limbo and the action cannot be retried until the request is cleared.  For the following scenarios, we will clear the stuck records after a set amount of time:
- If a workflow/step was kicked off over 2 hours ago and has yet to move on or finish, the system will automatically reset the step so it can be retried
- If an Excel (macro processing) or report generation request is stuck for over 2 hours without a response, the request will be reset and thrown back in the queue to be retried o If a FileID import has been in the queue for over 10 minutes without a result, the user who o
- initiated the import will be notified that the request was cleared and to retry
- Automation Setup
- Opt-In Automation - Shelf Check
- In order to enable the “Opt-in Automation” Other Setting, the deal must be assigned to a valid shelf (not blank or None_Shelf)
- If removing the setting, the deal must have a Processor and Reviewer assigned to it, i.e. it cannot be unassigned
- Workflow Setup - Access To Template Dropdown
- To place better controls over what deals can be automated, only Senior Managers have access to assign a workflow template to a deal now
- Update Copy From Logic for Processing Method
- When using the Copy From feature during workflow setup, it will no longer switch the Processing Method back to Manual – it will leave the Processing Method as-is.
- Copy From will continue to copy the steps, pre-conditions, validations and macros (and corresponding filemasks)
- New Validation - File Not Found
- A new validation option was created that that only fails if the desired file is found
- This validation can be used for CMBS supplemental data processing, where you may/may not get supplemental data for any given period
### Example:
- Enable the “Reprocess Supplemental Reports” workflow step if your deal requires supplemental data to be loaded.  If supplemental files expected by a certain date, set a Pre-Condition to match.
- Enable the File Not Found validation as a Pre-Validation on the step
- Filemask for {DID}_Comments_Load.xls
- When running the workflow, when it gets to the “Reprocess Supplemental Reports” step, ▪ If it finds the Comments file, it will fail.
- The fail is a reminder to the deal team to load the file, if they haven’t already done so.
### Once file is loaded, they can override the file validation fail and the step will move forward with regenerating the following RIDs, if applicable to the deal:
- 281 (Specially Serviced Loan Comment)
- 271 (Historical Loan Modification Report ▪ 464 (Breach Events Report) o If it doesn’t find the file, that can be taken to mean the file is not needed for that period o
- (nothing extra to load) so the validation will pass and step will move forward.
- Import Process
- Allow hardcoded maps for FileIDs
- Hardcoded maps are now allowed to be setup for FileIDs (Data-Actions > Setup > Servicer Setup > Import File Setup) and used with the LoadiMap_IR macro
- A prerequisite is the same map must be setup on the deal (under the Deal Maps section of the same screen)
- When loading the FileID via the UI or LoadiMap_IR, it will correctly record the MapID in tblImportLog and tblImportFileQueue and "blue" out the FileID row.
- Note: Some hardcoded maps were not coded to update tblImportLog, such as map 4.  In those cases, the FileID will not be recorded as imported even though the data was imported successfully.  o Recommend testing your hardcoded map in UAT to see if it updates tblImportLog or not.
- Import Exceptions - Keep Status As Finalized
- Once Accept Data is completed, the data status is “Finalized”
- As previously mentioned, some deals require supplemental data to be loaded that does not affect collateral or payment calculations, such as Special Servicing or Modification comments
- When importing into exception tables (tblCMSAComment and vwAgencyBreachReview), if Process Status is Finalized/Locked, it will remain that way because data does not need to be reprocessed o Previously, it would revert the status back to “Data Imported”, which would cause the Reviewer/Looksee Signoff or Deliver Final Reports step to fail
- Add Exception to Data Reviewed Check
### Similarly, when trying to load into 'tblCMSAComment' and 'vwAgencyBreachReview', as long as the workflow is at or before the Reprocess Supplemental Reports workflow step, you will no longer be denied with the following error:
- Basically, these exceptions for the specific tables will allow for the import of supplemental comments without unnecessary stops
- Note: Import into any other tables will continue to have the same stops and checks as before
- Post Import Process
- There are some maps, such as Map 1619, that trigger certain sprocs to run immediately after a successful import o If importing via iManage UI, the sprocs will run
- The most automated way we have to load files is to use the LoadiMap_IR macro. However, doing so would not trigger the same post import sprocs to be executed.
- The new SQL import process has been enhanced to execute the same sprocs.  However, only SQL maps can take advantage of this update.
- Automatic Workflow Kickoff
- Cloud Automation - Automatic Start w/ FileID Load
- If a deal is set to Cloud Automation, the workflow will now automatically kick-off as soon as all of the deal's Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs are loaded
- The only exception will be if there is a Pre-Condition set on the Begin Workflow step that has not been met yet.  In that case, the workflow will immediately kick off as soon as the PreCondition is met.
- Cloud Automation - Resume w/ Pre-Condition
- Under Cloud Automation, if a workflow had been halted due to a Pre-Condition, it will now automatically resume the step once the Pre-Condition date/time has been met
- Please double-check your FileID setup to ensure workflows don’t start until all your data is loaded.  Note: Optional (Not Expected) FileIDs should be rarely used, if at all.
- Please join one of Mike Ortiz’s scrubbing sessions if you use a data loader and are not sure how to handle an expected FileID that you know you will not need for any given period.
- Shelf Tables, Background and Screens
- New SQL Tables for Shelf Setup
- New SQL tables were created to house shelf and SME information o tblShelfSetup – shelf names and ShelfID o tblShelfTeamSetup – shelf SMEs and members
- The information displayed in Deal Setup > Basic tab pulls from these new tables
- Previously, shelf names and assigned SMEs were housed in tblMetricsDefaults
- The data for the new tables have been backfilled using the existing data in tblMetricsDefaults
- TOS updated various functions and sprocs to account for the changed tables, but if you run into any discrepancies related to shelf data, please report it.
- Note: SSRS reports and side tools were not updated. Business line should update those as needed.
- In the automated world, a shelf will not only have SMEs assigned to it, but also shelf members that can resolve exceptions as they arise.
- Shelf members may be assigned Processor, Reviewer or Looksee rights for that particular shelf
- Ex. A user who normally has Reviewer rights when processing legacy deals may not be knowledgeable enough about a shelf and may be assigned Processor rights on the shelf
- If a shelf-processed deal fails at Reviewer Signoff, that user will not be able to resolve the exception due to their limited (Processor) shelf rights
- To switch an automated deal to shelf-processing, unassign the deal in the Current Allocations tab o Note: Deal must be a part of a shelf that has members assigned to it or else the deal cannot be unassigned
- Three new tabs have been added to the Allocations screen to help manage shelves and shelf processing
- Shelf Management
- The Shelf Management tab will be used by shelf SMEs to assign members to their shelves
### For ease of reference the tab displays:
- Who the SMEs of the shelves are
- All the deals assigned to the shelf and if they are automated
- Only Shelf SME (new access group), Allocation Managers and Senior Managers can make edits on this screen o If a Shelf SME, they will only have access to edit their own shelf o All other users have view only access
- Once a shelf is selected, SMEs can select a user from the dropdown, hit Add User to Shelf to add them to the grid and update the Role for the user.  Once all members are added to the grid, hit Save to actually save the members to the shelf team. o Note: The EmailOptin feature for shelf members is not yet functional hence it is currently disabled
- For now, every member of the shelf team will be notified or cc:ed on emails that go out of iManage for the shelf-allocated deals
- The SME(s) are not automatically part of the shelf team.  If the SME wants to resolve issues, they must add themselves to the team as Looksee (highest level of rights).
- SME Management
### The SME Management tab should mainly be used by the Shelf Coordinator (new access group) to:
- Add/delete shelves
- Edit the names of existing shelves o Update SMEs assigned to each shelf
- Any changes saved to SME assignment on this tab will be reflected on the Shelf Management tab
- Note: Any change made to the grid will NOT actually change the data until the Save button is clicked.
- Only Shelf Coordinator, Allocation Managers and Senior Managers can make edits on this screen o All other users have view only access
- Temp Shelf Allocations
- Shelf SMEs can use the Temp Shelf Allocations tab to assign shelf-allocated deals within the selected shelf to shelf members for a selected period o Deals that are hard-allocated (assigned to specific users in the Current tab) are not eligible for temporary allocations and will not be displayed here
- The Processor/Reviewer/Looksee dropdowns are limited to the shelf member with the corresponding rights
- When changing the Effective Date dropdown, the results may differ depending on when the deals became shelf-allocated (unassigned in Current Allocations)
- Temporary allocations should be used when deals have exceptions o Once assigned, the deal can be treated as a hard allocation for that period only o For example, if Bear Stearns 2004-FR1 runs into a workflow fail for October 2022, the shelf SME can temporarily assign the deal to members Hoang, Suzy and Linda. o Come November, the deal will go back to be shelf-allocated
- If a deal is temp-allocated and is then hard-allocated to other users with the same effective date
- (for the same period), the temp assignments supersede the hard-allocations o Deal will appear for the users that it was temporarily assigned to and NOT for users that it was hard-allocated to
- Only Shelf SME (within their own shelf), Allocation Managers, and Senior Managers can set or modify temporary allocations o All others have view only access
- As with the other new tabs, any updates made to the grid will not actually go into effect until the Save button is clicked.
- Current Allocations
- Add Toggle for Automated vs. Non-Automated
- A toggle for Automated vs. Non-Automated was added to the Current Allocations screen
- As more deals get automated and with the advent of shelf-processing and all the rules that apply to them, it made sense to split the logic for this screen
- Logic for Non-Automated deals will work as it always has
- Rules for Allocating Automated Deals
- Allocations for automated deals will only apply on the Bond service type of the deal o Allocation type dropdown is intentionally disabled
### Can only unassign (assign to Not Avail.) automated deals if:
- o The deal is assigned to a valid shelf – not blank and not the None_shelf o The deal’s shelf has members assigned to it o All of the deal’s Initial Tasks have been completed
- Unassigning the Processor or Reviewer role will automatically unassign the other role o Ex. If Modify Processor to Not Avail. on a deal that is currently assigned to a Processor and Reviewer, both the Processor and Reviewer duties will get unassigned       Deal will become shelf-allocated
- If deal is currently assigned to a Processor, Reviewer and Looksee, can unassign the Looksee and the other allocations will remain
- If the deal is currently unassigned, must assign both the Processor and Reviewer to actual, separate users
- Shelf Processing
- My Deals Enhancements
- Quick Search
- When using the Quick Search feature, the users displayed will be based on whether the deal was temp vs. hard vs. shelf allocated for the selected period
- Ex. If deal was hard-allocated (assigned to users in the Current Allocations screen) for August 2022, Quick Search will show those users
- If deal was shelf-allocated starting in September 2022, Quick Search will display Shelf
- o Note: Refrain from clicking on the orange button for Shelf as it will take you to a random
- “Shelf” user view o Instead, figure out who is part of that deal’s shelf team and go under their view
- If deal was then temp-allocated for October 2022, Quick Search will display who those users are
- My Deals: Toggle for Individual Allocated vs. Shelf Allocated Deals
### Above the deals listing are radial buttons for:
- MyDeals – deals that are hard or temporarily allocated to you o Shelf – deals that are shelf-allocated to shelves that you are a member of
- Both the Incomplete and Complete sections will be driven by the toggle you select
- The first number listed next to MyDeals or Shelf lets you know how many within that category is Incomplete
- The second number is how many within the category has an Exception, such as a failed workflow step
- A tooltip has been added to the numbers so when you hover over them, it explains what the numbers represents
- Exceptions are also flagged with the letter E next to the DID so it’s clear which deals have problems to be resolved
- Using the same example as above with the Quick Search, o If deal was hard-allocated as of August 2022, deal will show under Theresa’s MyDeals view for that period
- If deal was shelf-allocated as of September 2022, deal will show under the Shelf view of all of the BS_SACO_shelf members for that period
- If deal was then temp-allocated for October 2022, deal will show under the MyDeals view of those users (Hoang and Suzy) for that period
- Assuming no other allocation changes are made, the deal will go back into the Shelf view of all of the BS_SACO_shelf members for November 2022 as the deal is back to being simply shelf-allocated
- Open Deal Folder
- The Open Deal Folder feature will now default to the monthly Deal Data Folder based on the period selected on the My Deals screen
- In addition, the shortcut to the U Deal Folder was added to account for backup servicing deals
- (see below for more details)
- Shelf Rights vs. iManage Rights
- Any member of a shelf team can kick off the workflow and any step for a deal within their shelf
- However, depending on what step an exception occurs on the shelf deal, o If user has Processor rights within the shelf, user cannot resolve exceptions that occur on
- Reviewer or Looksee steps o If user has Reviewer rights within the shelf, user cannot resolve exceptions on Looksee o
- Signoff o If user has Looksee rights within the shelf, no restrictions
- Shelf Processors are unable to revise shelf deals, even if they usually have elevated rights in iManage
- Shelf team rights overrides iManage rights – user with Senior Reviewer rights for iManage, but only Processor rights for a shelf will be limited by the Processor access when working on a shelf deal
- Shelf Email Notifications
### If a deal is shelf-allocated, the email notifications related to the deal will:
- Be sent to the shelf members and shelf SME(s) o List the shelf team/SME(s) in the body, if needed
- Note: Shelf members are cc:ed on these emails because that is the only record of the notification being sent to the third parties
- "Go-ahead" emails such as Ready to Process, Ready for Review and Ready for Final Review, will NOT go out if the deal is shelf allocated o The idea behind those emails is to let the next person know they can run the next step, but with automation, the next step would automatically be run by the automation engine.  Therefore, no one needs to be notified that it's their turn.
- Notification emails, such as when a step fails during Cloud Automation or if the workflow hits the Review Final Statement step, will be sent to all shelf members as additional action is required for the workflow to move forward
- Emails that go to parties outside of IR, such as when delivering files, revising a deal, large wires, swap amounts, insurance claims, etc., will
- Be cc:ed to the shelf members and SMEs
- May list the shelf team in case additional information is needed from IR
- IR Exceptions Management (IREM Dashboard)
- New Web-based Dashbaord
- From iManage’s Help menu, select IREM to log-on and open the new dashboard
- The IREM will open on Google Chrome with your profile encrypted in the URL
- o The characters after the key determines who the user is so please do not copy/share the
- URL that opens for you
- ▪ If you do, any actions taken by others using your profile will be recorded as being done by you
- The IREM gives an overview of the status of all automated deals for the selected period
- Please note that this is just the initial version of the IREM.  Many of the features, such as sorting and filtering by column, frozen headers, select all, etc. as well as formatting issues will be fixed in the next version.
- Features
- Filters
- If no filters are selected, the grid will display all the automated deals in alphabetical order
- As filters are selected, the grid will automatically refresh accordingly
- Each user can save their preferred filters.  Simply set each filter field as desired and hit Save Filter.  Going forward, each time you open the IREM or refresh the screen, the filters will reset to your saved settings.
- Note: The Sort By Status filter currently sorts in alphabetical order, but will be updated with Fails on top in the next release of the IREM
- Process/Revert/Stop
### If a deal is set to the Cloud Automation Processing Type, the IREM can be used to:
- Process the deal
- If the Required and Optional Expected FileIDs have not yet been loaded, the process will stop
- If the workflow has failed, you must first resolve the exception before attempting to Process
- Stop the deal if its workflow is currently “In Progress”
- The workflow will stop once the step it is currently on completes and it will not move onto the next step
- Revert Workflow
- As long as the step you’re trying to revert to is enabled for the deal
- Ex. Servicer sends new data for a shelf of deals.  Can select all the affected deals within the shelf and Revert their workflows back to Process Data in bulk.
- Refresh Deals
- To refresh the grid with the set filters to see the current status of the deal
### These action buttons can only be used on deals that you are hard/temp allocated to or if you are a member of the shelf that the deal belongs to o If you attempt to process a deal that you are not a part of, you will be denied:
- Multi-Process
- The IREM can be used to multi-process automated deals, as long as they are set to Cloud Automation
- Similar to how multi-process works in iManage for non-automated deals, you can kick off deals that are different steps in the workflow at the same time
- Grid
- If a deal has already been Delivered for the selected period, its checkbox will be disabled
- If a deal has failed, the Status Detail column displays the first few words of the error.  If you hover over the Status Detail, the tooltip will display the full error message.
- To get further details, click on the Exception Details hyperlink and it will open a form similar to the Step Report in iManage with full details o The format of the Exception Details will be fixed in the next version of the IREM
- Note: In order to view the data to the right of the grid, you must use the right arrow button on your keyboard.  This will be addressed in the next version of the IREM.
- Email Notifications
- As deals are processed through the IREM, if any of them fail,
- If deal is hard-allocated and users are opted into emails, those users will be notified of the fail
- If users are not opted into emails, they must refresh the IREM or check the deals in iManage to find out about the fails
- Please contact Linda Mai if you want to opt into emails
- If deal is temp or shelf allocated, the applicable shelf members will receive the email notification of the fail
- Simultaneous Runs
### If a user processes a deal via the IREM that someone else is also trying to process via iManage, the iManage user will get the following message:
- Workflow Processing
- Add Method Check to Main Button
- With shelf-processing, it is possible for multiple users to interact with the same deal at the same time
- If separate users attempt to change the Processing Method at the same time, the first one will be saved and the other user will be advised to refresh.
- This check will prevent the deal from being run simultaneously on two different queues
- New Process Tax Workflow Step
- A new workflow step called Process Tax has been added after the Deliver Final Reports step that will allow taxes to be processed immediately after a deal is bond processed
- Like with any other workflow step, o A Pre-Condition can be setup on the Process Tax step to not begin until a certain date/time each period
- o Pre and Post Validations can be enabled o Macros can be setup
- Exception Resolution
- If the Process Tax fails, an email notification will be sent to GSF IR Tax
- Only the Tax team can resolve exceptions on this particular step
- My Deals Enhancements
- Once the Deliver Final Reports step is completed successfully, the deal will move down to the Completed section
- If the Process Tax step is enabled on the deal, the deal will be marked with a red box to indicate the outstanding step
- The Automation tab will still be active, but the Revert To buttons will be disabled
- If the workflow needs to be reset, since the deal was already delivered, it will need to be
- Revised o If the Import/Load/Delete, Process or Accept Data buttons are clicked, you will still be required to Revise the deal in order to perform those actions since the deal has already been delivered
- Workflow Reset – Exception
- • You may recall that certain actions will reset active workflows, such as when workflow setup is changed o If Process Tax is the only outstanding step and the deal has already been delivered, any such actions will not reset the workflow and will only be implemented on future workflows
- Automation of Backup Services
- Setup Instructions
### Backup Serviced deals can also be automated, but requires special setup that must be done in the following order:
- In Deal Setup > Basic Info > Main Info tab, add the Bond service
- Assign deal to a valid shelf, i.e. not the None_Shelf o Please work with Backup Services SME/Shelf Coordinator to identify the appropriate shelf
### Work with Manager to make following changes in the Allocations > Current tab:
- Assign the Processor and Reviewer on the Bond level o Remove the allocations on the Backup Servicing level
### Work with a Senior Manager to:
- Flag the deal as Bond Reporting
- Assign the appropriate workflow template, such as the Bond Reporting template, to the deal
- ▪ Ensure that the workflow is setup on the Bond service
- In Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab o Enable any additional steps desired
- Setup desired pre-conditions, validations and macros on the enabled steps
- In Deal Setup > Other Settings, enable the “Opt-in Automation” setting o Now the deal will appear under the assigned users’ views under Bond and with the Automation tab enabled
- Open U: Deal Folder
- In the My Deals > Processing tab, the Open Deal Folder feature was updated to include the U: deal folder to account for the Backup Servicing deals that are automated under Bond
- As always, if you do not have access to the U: drive, you will not be able to access the folder
- Signoff Exceptions
- As long as the deal is flagged as Bond Reporting, it should not run into issues/fails at the signoff steps that normally run checks against the payment and tax ranges
- Miscellaneous
- Retraction Email Updates
- Instead of sending out two separate retraction emails when a deal is revised, we consolidated them into one email
- In addition, the email will be sent to all of the shelf’s SME(s) – not just the first one
- New CMBS Transaction Participants - Company Type for reporting on new deal
- Several new Company Type options were added in Advanced Settings to be displayed on the Table of Contents page under Parties to the Transaction: o Initial Special Servicer
- o Third Party Special Servicer o Sub-Custodian
- MCMLT Loss Trigger Review Event
- The Loss Trigger Review Event report logic was updated to only include current losses.
- Previously, it also included subsequent losses and recoveries.
- Bug fix in report logic for Prepayment & Liquidation Loan Detail (Full UPB) report
- For loans with a Payoff Code of 1 (Paid in Full), the deferred amount paid was being included in both the Prepayments Incl Curtail and then showing again in the Liquidation Proceeds column resulting in the report showing more funds received than the beginning balance.  This logic has been fixed.

- However, many of the Optional (Expected) FileIDs may not be needed for any given period so these deals can only be kicked off manually.
- To fill this gap, we can use a new sproc that will insert a record into our import tables for the FileIDs where data is not coming in so that the workflow engine is tricked into thinking that all the Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs have been loaded and workflow will kick off automatically.
- Please work with Mike Ortiz to integrate the sproc into your tools

- Version 7.0.0.9 (Release Date: 9/8/2022)
- Tuesday, March 7, 2023	3:53 PM
- Large Wire Check
- Non-Automated Deals
- Automated Deals
- Management of Cloud Services
- Additional Service Check / Automatic Switchover
- Two Servers Picked Up Same Request
- Deal Running in Both Local & Cloud Modes
- Automation Bug Fixes
- Automation Tab Buttons Disabled (Workflow Hadn't Started)
- Workflow Steps
- Generate Auto Report
- Package Report
- Processor Signoff
- Process Review
- Reviewer Signoff
- Loan Level CSV Files
- Large Wire Check
- The new reporting threshold requirement for incoming or outgoing wires has increased from $50 million to $100 million.
- Non-Automated Deals
- When filling out the large wire form, please remember to only answer Yes if the wire is more than $100 million.
### The email notification has been updated to reflect the change:
- Automated Deals
### The large wire check that was built into the Processor Signoff step was also updated:
- o If a tax range is setup in Deal Setup and is imported successfully, iManage will check to see if the following items are greater than $99,999,999.99
- 'ServicerCollections'
### 'Funds for Debt Service' ▪ 'No Transaction' ▪ Where the Grp is like:
- 'Servicer Remittance%’
- 'Available Funds%'
- 'Funds from underlying Securities%'
- 'Total%'
- o If so, it will automatically send the Large Wire notification stating there is “possibly” an incoming wire greater than $100 million coming
- Management of Cloud Services
### To limit the risk and downtime that outages/malfunctions in the various cloud services may cause, TOS implemented more checks:
- Additional Service Check / Automatic Switchover
- Whenever a command is sent to a server to run macros or generate reports, if the server fails to pass a preliminary access check, o The request will be put back in the queue so it can be picked up by another server o The service on the bad server will be stopped o Notification will be sent to TOS
- Example: If a server doesn’t have access to the J: drive and can’t access the Global Macros, that server will be stopped and the request will go to the next server that does have access.
- All of this will happen behind-the-scenes.  From an end user standpoint, the step/process may take a bit longer than expected due to the switchover to another server.  However, this will ensure that the step/process will be completed successfully.
- Two Servers Picked Up Same Request
- Previously, it was possible for two servers to pick up the same request, which resulted in simultaneous processing, mixed results and jumbled tracking.
- Now, as soon as a request is picked up by a server, the request will be locked down so no other servers may think the request is outstanding and needs to be worked on
- This enhancement was applied to both the Excel and Report services
- Deal Running in Both Local & Cloud Modes
- Previously, if multiple users loaded the same deal in the Automation tab with differing processing modes (ex. Cloud vs. Local Automation), it was possible for both methods to run and continue processing the workflow despite a fail.
- Now, once a workflow is kicked off, the processing mode will be locked down to the mode that was used when the workflow was kicked off
- This will ensure that any fails in the workflow actually stops the process.
- Automation Bug Fixes
- Automation Tab Buttons Disabled (Workflow Hadn't Started)
- Previously, after kicking off a deal’s workflow, if the user moved onto other deals to kick off their workflows, most of the buttons of the Automation tab would be disabled
- This refresh issue has been fixed and the Automation tab should be fully active as long as the deal’s workflow has not been completed yet.
- Workflow Steps
- Generate Auto Report
- On a day where we were experiencing heavy database blocking and slowness, the Auto Report step occasionally failed even though it seemed to generate everything correctly.
### The Auto Report API was updated to be better able to handle database slowness:
- If all reports generated and it is unable to capture metrics due to SQL blocking, it will skip the metrics capture
- If there are SQL issues during report generation, it will retry
- Package Report
- When a deal is setup with multiple custom views in a section, certain pages were being generated twice, but with different headers/overlays.
- Aspose was updated to handle this type of report setup correctly and distrib reports should generate correctly now.
- Processor Signoff
- If the deal is late, we should expect to have to fill out the Late form at Processor Signoff
- This was correctly happening when running the workflow in Manual and Local Automation mode, but not in Cloud Automation.
- Cloud Automation has been fixed to fail the Processor Step if a deal is late.
- If the deal team is opted in for emails, they will be notified of the fail and must complete the step in either Manual or Local Automation mode.
- Process Review
- The import of the payment/tax and review/trigger ranges would fail if the data was in Currency or Accounting format as Aspose couldn’t recognize the values.
- Aspose was updated to be able to handle those types of formats and should no longer fail to import.  No need for users to update the formats in their files.
- Reviewer Signoff
- The Reviewer Signoff step was consistently failing only in Cloud Automation mode.  This bug has been fixed.
- Linked Deals – The report sweeping logic was incorrectly naming the payment file for linked deals with the same payment date as the parent deal.  This caused the parent deal’s payments to never load into SDDB and the linked deal’s payments to load for the incorrect payment date.
- o This bug has also been fixed – separate payment files with the correct payment date in the file names will sweep for linked deals
- Loan Level CSV Files
- The headers in the Towd Loan Level Securitization.csv file that was not generating with the correct capitalization (to match legacy).  This bug is now fixed.
- The loan_id values in the regular Loan Level csv file was generating as “12345” instead of just 12345.  This bug is now fixed.
- Note: Both of these issues were reported by clients so please carefully review all reports and files generated by the new process to ensure everything matches legacy.

### The following importing bugs should be fixed, but please let us know if you continue to encounter these errors after the release:
- Queued Importing Fails - "Given source file does not exists" o When trying to import multiple files at once via the LoadiMap_IR macro, some of the attempts were failing with an error of "Given source file does not exists" even the source file does exists.
- TOS added some delays and implemented auto-retries if the process encounters this error, which should resolve the issue since manually loading the same file always works.
- Stuck Import – “Deal already processed/in progress for this Dt” o If a FileID load was previously attempted but never completed, the attempt would stay in limbo and iManage would not allow you to try to load the same FileID again.
### TOS added a check so that if it finds any limbo attempts within 10 minutes:
- It will auto-fail the attempt(s) to allow users to retry the load
- Send an email notification to TOS and deal team about the issue
- Failed Import Crashing iManage o Previously, failed FileID loads due to bad data/format in the source file would sometimes crash iManage and even display the file as being successfully loaded.
- Now, these failed loads will be displayed in the Deleted grid and iManage will stay open
- Display Actual FilePath vs. @StagingManualTemp o For better reference, the Loaded Data grid on the Import tab will now display the actual file path when loading FileIDs from the UI.  Previously it would display the file path as “M: \@StagingManualTemp\...”
- Auto Report - Fails for spExportLoanLevel3
- The Auto Report process (workflow step and ad-hoc button on the Export tab) can now export the TOWD Loan Level file, which was failing previously.
- ExportPayment Errors on Legacy Deals
### When cloud services went down, Processor and Reviewer Signoff for non-automated deals, including UK deals, were unexpectedly affected with an erroneous Global Macro error:
- The legacy code was fixed to be able to complete Processor and Reviewer Signoffs, including the import of payment/tax and review/trigger data, without issues if the cloud services go down
- Note: If using the Payments tab to Add payment/tax and review/trigger ranges, will get the following error, which can be ignored.
- After hitting OK, iManage will still import the data
- Cloud Services Health Check
- As we continue to move our processes outside of iManage, we have experienced outages due to those services being down.  To limit the risk and downtime that these outages may cause, TOS has implemented various ways to check the health of the services at all times.  If services go down,
- An email notification will automatically be sent to TOS with details so they can start troubleshooting immediately
- The next time the service is called upon, users will get a clear message of the problem.
### When running a step that calls on the service:
### When hitting a button that calls on the service:
### When service is called via Cloud Automation:
- Note: The check assumes that services are “healthy” if they ran successfully in the last 2 minutes.  Therefore, if the service is called immediately after it goes down, it will still attempt the process that was called. An additional 10-minute timeout was built into the process so that if we don’t get a response back from a service within 10 minutes, the step/process will fail and TOS should be notified.
- Automation Enhancements
- Workflow Setup
- Numerous updates were made to the Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab.
- Note: If there is an active workflow for any period, making changes in the Workflow Setup screen will reset any active workflows back to Begin Workflow.
- Default Processing Method
### Deal teams can set the "Default Processing Method" to Manual or Local Automation, however the option of Cloud Automation can only be set if:
- The Final 6 Month Review is completed on the deal
- And the person attempting to change it to Cloud Automation is assigned to the deal, the deal shelf's SME or an Admin
### These restrictions have been implemented in both the:
- Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab
- My Deals > Automation tab
- Service Type
- The Service Type dropdown is limited to the non-tax duties that are assigned to the deal.
- Only one of the deal’s services may be automated.
- Copy From
- • The Copy From feature was enhanced to copy the Pre-Condition, Pre-Validation, PostValidation and Macro setup from the source deal. o Previously, the feature only copied the workflow steps over.
- Macro Setup
- • The macros are now listed in alphabetical order for easier setup.
- Allocation Check at Save
- When selecting a template or enabling/disabling Processor, Reviewer or Looksee Signoff workflow steps on a deal, iManage will check to make sure the same duties have been assigned in the Allocations screen.
- If a discrepancy is found, a message will pop to remind you to fix the discrepancy.
- Mandatory Macros/Validations
- If a new mandatory macro/validation is added to a workflow step, it will automatically be enabled on all deals with the step enabled.
- If a macro/validation will no longer be mandatory on a workflow step, it will automatically be removed from all deals that have the step enabled.
- These updates are handled by a trigger so changes do not have to be made on individual deals that have already been setup for automation.
- Step Report Updates
- Access Check - Based on User’s Role
- When a deal is automated, the assigned Processor is allowed to trigger the automation engine to run all the workflow steps.
### However, the below steps have certain restrictions:
- Prepare Review o Process Review o Check Report - Reviewer o Signoff - Reviewer o Signoff – Looksee
- If a user form, such as the Going Green Tasks, Termination or Late forms, are triggered on the above steps, the Processor cannot complete the form
- The Processor cannot skip any macros on the above steps before running the steps
- The Processor cannot override failed validations or resolve any exceptions on the above steps
### If the Processor attempts to complete the forms, they will get denied:
- Only users that have the rights to signoff as Reviewer in the legacy world can perform the Processor-restricted actions on the listed steps.
- However, if the above steps pass all of their validations, macros and business logic, the Processor is allowed to trigger the next workflow step.
- Step Check on Unlock Button
- If the deal is automated and has an active workflow for ANY period that is at Process Distrib or later, hitting the Unlock button on the My Deals > Processing tab will trigger a warning that continuing will wipe out all signoffs and revert the workflow back to the Process Distrib workflow step.
- If the active workflow(s) is prior to the Process Distrib step, unlock will proceed without issue
- New Large Wire Check
- The Large Wire form was removed from the Begin Workflow, Processor/Reviewer/
- Looksee Signoff workflow steps
- If the "Skip Large Wire" setting is enabled in Deal Setup > Other Settings, it will skip the new large wire check
### The new check was built into the Processor Signoff step, based on the values imported from the tax range:
- If a tax range is setup in Deal Setup and is imported successfully, iManage will check to see if the following items are greater than $49,999,999.99
- 'ServicerCollections'
### 'Funds for Debt Service' ▪ 'No Transaction' ▪ Where the Grp is like:
- 'Servicer Remittance%’
- 'Available Funds%'
- 'Funds from underlying Securities%'
- 'Total%'
- o If so, it will automatically send the Large Wire notification stating there is “possibly” an incoming wire greater than $50 million coming
- If a tax range is setup, but the above items were not imported, the Processor Signoff will fail until the items are added to the tax range.
- If the deal is flagged for Bond Reporting and the tax range is not setup, the large wire check will be skipped.
- Workflow Steps
- More steps were added to the workflow and existing steps were enhanced
- Accept Data
- The negative remittance check that was built into Accept Data and would trigger a reminder/acknowledgement pop-up has been removed (from both the workflow step and the Process > Discrepancy > Accept Data button)
- For automated deals, the check will be done as a mandatory Post-Validation on the Accept Data step
- Prepare Distrib
- The Prepare Distrib step has been integrated into the workflow.
- There is no business logic for the step, but you may setup pre-conditions, pre/post-validations and macros on the step.
- Use case is insured deals that run UpdateCas_IR twice.  Can run the first round of macros on the distrib at the Prepare Distrib step to run calculations through the waterfall and the second round of macros at the Process Distrib step to calculate guarantor payments to cover shortfall amounts, insurance claims, etc. .
- Package Report
- • Agency Supplemental Loss and Modification Reports have been integrated into the automated packaging process o The individual Excel reports as well as the zipped file will be generated at the Package
- o
- Report workflow step and the Extract Templates button in the Process > Export tab
- Check Report – Processor
- The step formally known as Processor Going Green or Processor Tasks has been integrated into the workflow on the Automation tab
- The step should coincide with the Ongoing Tasks setup o If the Going Green tasks are setup in Deal Setup > Ongoing Tasks, but the Check Report – Processor step is not enabled, a check at Deliver Final Reports will fail
- If the workflow is running in Local or Cloud Automation, when it gets to this step, automation will stop and the mode will change to Manual.
- If workflow is running Cloud Automation, you will NOT be notified that it stopped at the step.  You must refresh the deal in iManage to see that it is at the step.
- Users must complete this step manually in iManage
- Once all tasks are completed, the forms will auto-close and step will be marked as Complete
- If forms are closed prior to all tasks being completed, the step will be marked as a Fail
### A couple of things to note:
- The Tasks form in the Automation takes a little longer to auto-close than usual.  Please be patient and give it time to close on its own.

- Prepare Review
- The Prepare Review step has been integrated into the workflow.
- There is no business logic for the step, but you may setup pre-conditions, pre/post-validations and macros on the step.
- Check Report – Reviewer
- The step formally known as Reviewer Going Green or Reviewer Tasks has been integrated into the workflow on the Automation tab
- The step should coincide with the Ongoing Tasks setup o If the Going Green tasks are setup in Deal Setup > Ongoing Tasks, but the Check Report – Reviewer step is not enabled, a check at Deliver Final Reports will fail
- If the workflow is running in Local or Cloud Automation, when it gets to this step, automation will stop and the mode will change to Manual.
- If workflow is running Cloud Automation, you will NOT be notified that it stopped at the step.  You must refresh the deal in iManage to see that it is at the step.

- Once all tasks are completed, you must manually close the Tasks form and step will be marked as Complete
- If forms are closed prior to all tasks being completed, the step will be marked as a Fail
- Signoff – Reviewer
- The step logic was updated to only check for the Review sheet PDF file in the T: folder if Going Green Reviewer tasks are enabled on the deal
### It was also updated to not try to export the payment file:
- o If deal is flagged as Bond Reporting and doesn’t have the payment/tax ranges setup o OR if deal doesn’t have the payment file setup in Deal Setup > Files
- Reprocess Supplemental Reports
- After Reviewer Signoff, some deals (primarily CMBS) need to import comments files and regenerate the report pages related to those comments o In the legacy world, after importing the comments, deal teams must repackage and redo their Processor/Reviewer Signoffs
- Reprocess Supplemental Reports is a new workflow step that was created for this scenario so prior signoffs don’t have to be redone
### Current recommended setup of the step:
- Enable the step via Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab
- If the file usually comes on a certain date, setup a Pre-Condition to coincide with that date so the step won’t even try to process if it hasn’t met that date yet
### Enable the following pre-validations:
- Deal Team must manually validate
- Does File Exist with filemask of the comments file
- Note: Table specific validations are being requested to determine whether the comments are required are not.  In the future, these validations could be used instead, but for now, it will have to be determined by the deal team, hence Deal Team must manually validate.
### How it works:
### The Reprocess Supplemental Reports step will:
- Fail at the Pre-Validation stop to allow deal teams to import the comments.  Once the comments are imported, deal team can override the fail via the Step Report
- Check to see if the comments file exists
- If yes, Does File exists validation will be marked as success
- If no, validation will fail to remind deal teams to follow-up on the file
### o Importing allowed (without risk of reverting workflow) for maps that load into tblCMSAComment and vwAgencyBreachReview o Once the comments are loaded and deal team overrides the above pre-validation, the step o regenerates the following RIDs, if applicable to the deal:
- 281 (Specially Serviced Loan Comment)
- 271 (Historical Loan Modification Report
- 464 (Breach Events Report)
- Reprocess Distrib
- Similarly, some deals need to reprocess their distribs, such as for next rates, in order to update custom views/distrib reports and regenerate the report pages related to those changes o In the legacy world, deal teams must unlock inputs to refresh and export, reprocess distribs, repackage and redo their Processor/Reviewer Signoffs
- Reprocess Distrib is a new workflow step that was created for this scenario so prior signoffs don’t have to be redone
### Current recommended setup of the step:
- Enable the step via Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab
- For next rates or similar scenarios, setup a Pre-Condition to coincide with the date/time the next rate usually loads so the step won’t even try to process if it hasn’t met that date/time yet
- Enable the macros
- ▪ InputReprocess_IR
- This macro should only be used with the Reprocess Distrib workflow step.  It will refresh inputs so users don’t have to unlock, refresh and export manually. o If next rate is loaded, it will come through o No input will be allowed to be blank – if so, fail o If all good, will export the inputs
- ▪ Import_IR and/or whatever is required in order to reprocess the distrib as needed
### How it works:
### o The Reprocess Distrib step will:
- Fail if the Pre-Condition has not been met yet
- • If rates are loaded prior to the date/time set, deal teams can manually trigger the step to process
- If a Pre-Condition was not setup and the InputReprocess_IR macro finds that the next rates have not been loaded yet, the macro will fail
- Once the next rate is into the database, can retry the step and the
- InputReprocess_IR macro will pull the next rate came into the Input Manager screen
- (without users having to unlock/refresh)
- If there are no other blank inputs, the macro will also export the CasInput file into the T: folder
- All other macros setup on the step will reprocess the distrib
- Repackage Report
- Repackage Report is a new workflow step that regenerates the final package to merge together the revised component pages created by the Reprocess Supplemental Reports and/or
- Reprocess Distrib steps with the rest of the original component pages o CMBS example: It will create a new package with only the Special Servicer and Modification pages replaced.
- The step has two mandatory macros attached to it: o PmtChangeCheck_IR
- Compares a snapshot of the custom views during the original Package Report step to the current custom views
- If any number changed besides a percentage/rate, the macro will fail and refer users to the CVChangeCheck file exported to T:\ISERV\{did} so deal teams can troubleshoot.
- The macro also checks to make sure payments haven’t changed since the original package
- Compares the payment range in the current distrib to snapshot of tblPmtInfo (previously loaded) - if different, fail
- Compares the tax range in the current distrib to snapshot of tblProcessinData
- (previously loaded) - if different, fail
- o ReportPackage_IR
- ▪ If PmtChangeCheck_IR is successful, only then will the final package be regenerated with the revised pages by this macro
- Note: Even though these steps follow Reviewer Signoff, Processors are able to resolve exceptions in the Reprocess Supplemental Reports, Reprocess Distrib and Repackage Reports steps – Reviewers don’t need to get involved.
- Review PDF
- After the final package is regenerated, the Review PDF step can be enabled to allow users to manually check the report before delivery.
- The step can only be run in Manual mode o If workflow is being run in Cloud Automation, deal team members who are opted-into emails will get an email instructing them to run the step manually
- Step will open a PDF-XChange Viewer with the regenerated final package (just like with the Check Report – Processor step)
- o The PDF can be checkmarked, but this marked version will not be saved anywhere o Once the PDF-XChange Viewer is manually closed, you will be asked if you want to continue
- Yes – the workflow will continue to Delivery Signoff step (or Looksee Signoff, if applicable)
- No – the step will be marked as a Fail
- Deliver Final Reports
- The step was updated for Additional File Deliveries that are setup in Deal Setup > Files
- If the additional file delivery fails, the step will fail with details
- The Deliver Final Reports step was also updated to account for the regenerated package created by the new steps o Existing logic - if the final package has changed since Reviewer Signoff, the step will fail o However, with the addition of the reprocess/repackage steps, the package has obviously been updated since Reviewer Signoff
- New logic for deals that have the reprocess/repackage steps enabled is to only fail if the final package was updated after the Review PDF step was completed
- Automation - Miscellaneous
- Update Failed Automation Email Format
- The email notifications triggered by failed workflow steps run by the cloud have been updated for easier reference.
- In the Error Details column, the first line (green) will explain the problem in layman’s terms whereas the bottom section (blue) will display the technical details that can be given to TOS for troubleshooting.
- Automation Tab Disabled When Deal Complete
- • Once all of the deal’s workflow steps are complete, the Automation tab will effectively be disabled.  Deal must be Revised. o The signoff button will display Success and be deactivated o The Revert To buttons will be hidden

### The Auto Report button on the Data-Actions > Process > Export tab was updated:
- Step Check
- If deal is already complete for the selected period, you will no longer be able to Auto Report - "Deal must be revised in order to Auto Report.  Use the Export button to export individual reports."
- In addition, if deal is automated, you will not be allowed to Auto Report via the ad-hoc button if the workflow is past the Generate Auto Report step.  You will have to revert back to the step and run Auto Report via the workflow step instead.
- If deal is automated, it will use the new Auto Report process/logic (described below as part of the Generate Auto Report workflow step)
- If deal is not automated, it will continue to use the existing built-in iManage process
### No more freezing – when Auto Report is done:
- A black box message will appear on the bottom right corner of the screen stating the process is complete
- Screen should automatically refresh with all the buttons and fields activated again
- CR Reports for PDF Package – similarly, when running CR Reports from the My Deals > Run feature, the black box message stating that it’s in progress will disappear once it’s done and iManage should refresh automatically
- Create Sample Package
- The Create Sample Package options in the My Deals > Run feature will now utilize the new cloud-based process to generate the package.  You should notice no difference in the output.
- Old Packaging Features
### As previously mentioned, the below features have all been removed from iManage:
- Deal Setup > Other Settings > “Old Packaging Method”
### My Deals > Processing > Run options:
- o Reports to Excel o Distrib to PDF o iRibbon Excel Package
- Excel checkbox next to Package PDF button
- Load FileID
- The Loaded Data grid on the Data-Actions > Process > Import tab was fixed to display the actual file path in the File Path Name instead of the “/tmp/mdrive…” path.
- Data-Actions > Load button was updated to keep the status as Data Imported for CMBS deals after loading a file.  It was incorrectly changing the status to Finalized.
- Automation Enhancements
- Workflow Setup
- Numerous updates were made to the Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab, including the name of the setup form that updates to reflect the step that is being setup.
- Note: If there is an active workflow for any period, making changes in the Workflow Setup screen will reset the workflow back to Begin Workflow.  Ex. If you make workflow setup changes after a deal has already been signed off by the Processor, it will wipe out all signoffs and revert back to Begin Workflow for that period.
### Pre-Condition:
- In the Pre-Condition setup form, the Date Code Legend (hover) feature was added that displays the legend for easy reference.
- In addition, a Delete button was added to remove any pre-condition that were previously setup on a step and no longer needed.
- Pre or Post Validations
- • Once certain workflow steps are enabled on a deal, mandatory validations will automatically be added to the steps.  You will not be able to remove mandatory validations.
- Macros
- The Macro column was added to allow you to setup macros on each workflow step.
- Similar to the legacy Macro Manager screen, you can use the Filter Tree to search for a macro
- Double-click on the desired macro under the library to add it to the step
- When adding a Custom Macro, be sure to update the MacroName to match the custom macro name that needs to be run
- Certain steps, such as Process Review, will automatically have mandatory macros enabled and cannot be removed from the step. The mandatory macros will always be run after any userenabled macros on the step.
- You can change the order in which the macros should be run by updating the number in the Order column
- Note: You will notice that all the macros that are listed in the legacy Macro Manager screen under the “iManage” category are not available in the new macro library.  Instead of being run by a macro, simply enable those steps in the workflow and they will be run by automation.
- Step Report Updates
- When expanded, the form name will automatically update to reflect the step that is being viewed.
- A tooltip was added to the Result Message field so you can view the entire message when you hover over it.  You can also copy the details out.
- If you have multiple file validations setup on a step, the report will list the exact file that failed in the File Path field.
- If a validation fails that you believe can be ignored, you may flag the Override Fail checkbox for the validation.  The column was previously named Accept Result.
- Override Fail cannot be checked prior to the validations being run.
- Depending on which workflow step an exception occurs, certain users will not have the ability to override fails or skip macros.
- The assigned Processor cannot resolve exceptions/fails that occur on review or looksee steps.
- The assigned Reviewer cannot resolve exceptions/fails that occur on the looksee step.
- Once you make your selections of Override Fail or Skip (in the Macros tab), hitting Accept & Resume will automatically trigger the workflow to continue in whatever processing mode it was running in (Manual, Local Automation or Cloud Automation)
- Note: Once a step is completed, all the fields in the Step Report for that field will be locked down.
- Queue Check
### Since multiple users may try to kick off automation on a deal, a queue check will be done at the following places:
- Apply & Resume button on the Step Report – if someone else had already resolved the exception on the step you are trying to resolve, you will get a message that "Workflow no longer at this step.  Please refresh the screen to see current status."
- Main workflow execution button on the Automation tab – if someone had already kicked off the workflow step that you want to kick off, you will get the same message.
- At OK, the UI will auto-refresh and display the step the deal is actually at
- Automation Macro Manager
- For automated deals, macros will be run on a server, instead of your machine.
- If, for some reason, the server is unable to run macros, it will time out after 10 minutes.  If you get the following fail, please notify GSF IR Support immediately.
- Similar to the legacy Macros form, you may Skip macros prior to running the workflow step by opening the Step Report for the step and flagging the applicable macro.
- However, mandatory macros cannot be skipped.  Any failed mandatory macro must be corrected until the macro passes.
- If a macro fails, the Result Message will provide details, which can be copied out for easier reference.
- Revisions
- Revision Stamp
- When revising a deal, you will get a pop-up asking if you want to include the Revision stamp on the package.
- Answering the question prior to running the workflow through automation will prevent an unnecessary stop in the process.
- However, if it’s decided that the Revision stamp is (or is no longer) needed, you can change your selection via the Revision Stamp checkbox on the Automation tab.
- The checkbox will only be editable while workflow is in the Begin Workflow through
- o
- Generate Auto Reports step.  Once Auto Report is completed, the checkbox will be uneditable.
- If you need to change your stamp selection after generating the revised package, you will need to revert back to the Generate Auto Reports step
- Refresh after Revisions
- The Automation tab will show that most of the signoffs have been cleared for the revised period, depending on the type of revision.
- If due to Servicer, workflow will be reverted back to Begin Workflow
- If due to any other reason, workflow will be reverted back to the first enabled step after Auto Report
- Even though the processing method may be Local or Cloud Automation, the workflow will not begin after a revision until you manually kick it off via the signoff button on the Automation tab
### The Data-Actions screen’s status will also be updated based on the revision reason:
- If due to Servicer, status will be updated to “Data Imported” o If due to any other reason, status will be updated to “Processed”
- Step Check on Payments Tab
- If the deal is automated, importing the payment/tax and review/trigger ranges via the Add buttons on the My Deals > Payments tab may be restricted, based on where the deal is in the workflow.
- If deal has already been sent, the Tax team may Add the ranges as needed for tax purposes
- If deal is at Processor Signoff or later, hitting Add under the Report Info will trigger a warning that continuing will wipe out all signoffs and revert the workflow back to Processor Signoff.
- If deal is at Reviewer Signoff or later, hitting Add under the Review Info will trigger a warning that continuing will wipe out signoffs and revert the workflow back to Reviewer Signoff.
- Workflow Steps
- More steps were added to the workflow and existing steps were enhanced
- Generate Auto Reports
### The Generate Auto Reports workflow step will now do everything that the Auto Report button does as well as generate any Crystal components that are masked for the Support Package:
- Export remittance reports to the T: drive o Export text files to T: drive o Export Final Package components
- ▪ Note: If running the step in Manual or Local Automation mode, you may notice that it is generating every few pages – this is due to multi-threading.  Rest assured that each component page is being generated.
- Export Support Package Crystal components
- If for some reason, the server is unable to run generate reports, it will time out after 10 minutes.  If you get the following fail, please notify GSF IR Support immediately.
- Process Distrib
- After all macros setup on the step are successfully run, iManage will import the payment and tax ranges.
- Prior to importing the payment data, it will first confirm that the Month/Year range in the distrib matches the selected period for earlier detection of an issue.
- Tip! If a new item is added to your tax range, it must be added to the tblImportSetup in order for iManage to successfully import the data.  Please be sure to submit an iTracker ticket to add the new item to the tax range options.
- Package Report
- To prevent having to go back to repackage if a terminated deal needs the Disclosures page to report holdback funds, iManage will check to see if a deal is possibly terminating at this workflow step o If the bonds pay down to $0, the Termination form will pop
- o If you confirm that holdback funds are required, the Disclosures page will be generated and merged as part of the Final Package
- The Package Report step will create both the Support Package and the Final Package o If deal is automated, the Package PDF and Supp Package buttons on the My Deals >
- o
- Processing tab will be disabled.
- As mentioned above, the Revision Stamp must be determined prior to the Generate Auto Reports step.  It will not pop at the Package Report step as it currently does on the Package PDF button.
- Signoff – Processor
- • For deals with insurance claims, previously if the Account Admin was not setup on a deal, the step would continue.  This will now be considered a fail and the AA must be added via the Contacts screen in order for the step to proceed successfully.
- Process Review
- After all user-enabled macros are run on this step, MasterCheck_IR will be run as a mandatory macro
- If all macros are run successfully, iManage will import the review and trigger ranges.  If discrepancies found when comparing to the payment and tax range, the Discrepancy Report will be exported to the T: drive with the details. o Note: The Discrepancy Report will be a html file that opens on a browser.
- Signoff – Reviewer
- • If iManage is unable to pull the data for the following files, which are generated at the Reviewer Signoff, the step will fail.  In legacy world, the files would be skipped. o CUSIP
- o Pool level o Load level o Bond summary o Collateral summary
- Signoff – Looksee
- This step was changed to be an automatic step so as long as all built-in checks and validations pass, the Looksee Signoff step may be completed by automation
- If the review/trigger ranges are missing for whatever reason, iManage will import the review and trigger ranges and perform the discrepancy check against the payment/tax range and export a Discrepancy Report to the T: drive, if needed.
- Deliver Final Reports
- A mandatory pre-validation of “Human check required” is enabled on the last step of the workflow o If all the workflow steps complete without issues, management would like a person to still review the deal manually while we are in the early stages of automation
- o This pre-validation will force the workflow to stop to allow users to review the deal before sending the deal out
### The following checks on this step, fka Send, are slightly different from what happens with nonautomated deals:
- If the Final Package modified date is greater than the Reviewer Signoff or Review PDF signoff, the step will fail
- If the payment file or reports fail to be delivered, the step will fail
- Cloud Automation
- For now, you must manually trigger Cloud Automation to start by clicking on the "Begin
- Workflow" button o All Required FileIDs must be loaded
- o If there are Optional (Expected) FileIDs setup on the deal, you will have to confirm that you want to proceed without them being loaded
- If Yes, automation will begin in the cloud
- If No, it will continue to wait until the Optional (Expected) FileIDs are loaded
- Once Cloud Automation is working consistently, a future update will allow it to automatically kick off once all Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs are loaded – no user intervention will be needed
- Email Notifications
- Similar to legacy deals, if you are opted-in for emails, you will receive automatic notifications whenever the deal is ready for you
- If the deal is running in Cloud Automation mode and fails for any reason, all users that are assigned to the deal and are opted-in for emails will get the failure notification with details of the step that failed
- Reset
- If you deal seems to be unexpectedly stuck, for more than 10 minutes, you may reach out to
- GSF IR Support to have them Reset the step that your deal is on
