- Packaging Update
- The utilities that iManage historically used to overlay the report header/footer on pages, merge pages, number pages, create the Table of Contents, add links/ revision stamps/watermarks, etc. were replaced with AsposePDF.
- All of the following features are now using AsposePDF and although there shouldn’t be any difference, PLEASE PAY ATTENTION to the generated reports.
- Report any issues immediately!
- Package PDF
- Support Package
- Create Sample Package
- ZIP It Feature
- As part of the modernization effort, the ZIP It feature in the My Deals > Investor Files tab was updated to remove unused utilities.
### For any completed period, it will zip all the files listed on the tab into a zip file in the deal’s J:
- \{dealfolder}\PDF folder.
- Automation Enhancements
- Pre-Conditions
- Once workflow steps are enabled on a deal, you can set a “Pre-Condition” on any desired step(s) that instructs the workflow engine to not start that step until the Date/Time indicated.
### How to setup a Pre-Condition:
- In the Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab, click on the button under the PreCondition column in the row for the applicable step
- Populate the Country Code and Country Code Adj (Optional) o If unsure of the LOCODE, click on the button on the right of the related cell to open the Country Code form  o If the Country Code and Country Code Adj is left blank, it will be saved with a default of
- NYC, NYC
- Populate the Date Code (Required) o Setup a valid date code.  In a future release, the Date Code Legend will be added to the Pre-Condition form.
- Time in HH:MM AM/PM format (Optional)
- o If left blank, it will be saved with the default of 12 AM
- In the above example, the Signoff – Reviewer step would not kick off until 2 business days prior to the 25th at 10 AM CST.
### Tip: Use DateCode_IR macro to verify your date codes will be calculated correctly:
- Pre or Post Validations
- Once workflow steps are enabled on a deal, you can set validations on any desired step(s) that instructs the workflow engine to run some checks at the beginning or end of each step.
- Setup
- In the Deal Setup > Processing > Workflow tab, click on the button under the PreValidation/Post Validation column in the row for the applicable step
- In the setup form, all validations applicable to the step will be displayed on top.
- Depending on whether you activated the form from the PreValidation or PostValidation column, different options may be available (based on what makes sense) o Click on ADD on the desired validation that you want to enable on your deal’s step
- You can filter by Category by dragging the header up to help find your desired validation quicker
- Note: There is a “Deal Team must manually validate” option that doesn’t check for anything, but will stop the step so deal teams can review the deal before choosing to resume the workflow. File Validations
- Blank File – checks the file size and if it’s less than 5 kb (default), it may be blank.
- Current File – checks the file is no more than 15 days old (default).
- Does File Exist – checks to see if the file exists.
- The same file validation can be enabled multiple times as long as the file path is different for each.  Ex. it can be used to check that each of the supplemental files were saved in the correct location and/or are current.
- If enabled, the FilePath must be populated.  Filemasks work.
- The Current File and Blank File validations can be customized to check based on different thresholds than the DefaultValues of 15 days or 5 kb, respectively.
- SQL-Based Validations
- Aside from the file and “Deal Team must manually validate” validation options, the rest of the validations are based on SQL queries.
- SQL validations are categorized as either Bond, Collateral or Report validations.
- Depending on the validation, some may be specific to the deal type: Agency, Bond, CMBS or
- All.
- Some validations are mandatory, depending on the step.  These are the same checks that iManage used to do and you would have to acknowledge during signoffs.
- The related sproc name with the logic for each validation is listed for easy reference.
- Tip: If you have ideas for additional validations, feel free to add them to the GSF IR >
- Automation-Validations channel
- After saving your selections, the main grid will display the number of items you enabled per step. You may click on the related button to get the details.
- Exception Resolutions
- After setting up Pre-Conditions, Pre or Post Validations, whenever the deal’s workflow steps are run, the workflow engine will perform the requested checks and provide feedback via the My Deals > Automation Tab and Step Report, where you can “resolve” some of the exceptions.
- When running the deal in Manual or Local Automation mode, the Workflow Status form will display the progress of each step and the main grid will indicate which task within the step failed.
- To get more details of exactly what failed, highlight the step and expand the Step Report.  It will open to the task’s tab that failed.
- After fixing the issue(s), simply re-run the step and the validations will run again and hopefully pass.
- However, if you confirm that the step can continue despite the validation fail (there is nothing to fix), you can checkmark the Accept Result box for the validation(s) that failed.  Hit Apply and rerun the step. The workflow engine will consider that prior fail a pass now based on your confirmation.
- Similarly, if the set Pre-Condition date/time has not been met yet, but you want to continue the workflow anyway, you can do so from the Step Report.
- Generate Auto Reports Step
- Auto Report functionality has been integrated into the Generate Auto Reports workflow step.  The work is all done on a server using updated services, but the results are the same as the historical method.
### At Auto Report, it will:
- Export reports and text files to the T:\ISERV\{DID} folder o If additional export locations set, text files will be exported there as well
- Export package reports to the T:\ISERV\{DID}\PackagePDF folder
- Auto Report will not work if the deal is in Processed or Partial Acceptance status
- Cloud Automation
- Automation can now kick off on its own and be run in the cloud for all of the integrated steps: Begin Workflow, Process Data, Accept Data, Check Remit, Generate Auto Reports, Signoff – Processor, Signoff – Reviewer, and Signoff - Looksee.
- Prerequisites
- At least one Required FileID must be setup
- Processing Method set to Cloud Automation (in either Deal Setup or Automation tab)
- How it Works
- If the processing method is set to Cloud Automation, a service will check for the moment that all of the deal’s Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs have been loaded.  Once loaded, the workflow will automatically start.
- If data is loaded via automated processes (ex. Active Batch), as long as they are loaded via the FileIDs, no human interaction is needed.
- Note: If data is imported using the old Import button, it will NOT be counted.
- If all of the deal’s workflow steps run successfully, it will stop at Deliver Final Reports (fka Send) and change the method back to Manual.
- Since this is new, we are requiring that users do a manual review of the deal prior to sending.
- ▪ Once confidence is built for the process, we will automate the final delivery as well.
- Similarly, if the Signoff – Looksee step is enabled, the workflow will stop and change to Manual.  Deals that need Looksee should be reviewed by the Final Reviewer.
- If a step fails during cloud automation, the process will stop and you will have the opportunity to resolve the issue and then retrigger the cloud automation. o This includes any possible user forms you may need to interact with, such as Large Wire, Termination or Late forms.
- Opt-In Email Notifications
- • If you are opted in to receive email notifications from iManage, you will get an email if a step fails during cloud automation with details.
- Automation Tab Controls
- The My Deals > Automation tab can be used to see the progress of the cloud automation.
- If your deal’s Required FileID has been loaded, but you are not going to get your Optional (Expected) FileID, you can manually kick off cloud automation by clicking on the Begin Workflow button.
- As the deal is running, you can hit the Refresh button to see the latest progress.
- As the deal is running, you can hit the Stop button to stop the progress.  Note: it will finish all of the step’s tasks (pre-condition, pre-validation, step logic, and post-validation) and then stop.  It cannot step in the middle of the step.
- Allocation Check
- In the Allocations screen, when users hit the Update button, iManage will check if the deal is automated and compare the requested allocations to the deal’s enabled workflow steps.
- o Check will only be done Bond, Backup Servicing or Fund Accounting deals
- If selected automated deal(s) doesn't have the related signoff step enabled, the Update will fail.
- The deals and details of the fail will automatically be copied to your Office clipboard. You can immediately paste the details to troubleshoot.
### Same check was applied to the bulk transfer feature:
- Other Enhancements
- User Forms Reminder
- When running the workflow in Manual or Local Automation mode, you may be presented with different user forms, such as the Large Wire, Termination or Late forms.
- If you expand your VDI over multiple monitors, those user forms may appear on a monitor that is different from the one iManage is open on.
- When hitting Stop on a step, the process may appear stuck because there is a user form open that you didn’t notice.
- o The stop verbiage will remind you to acknowledge any outstanding user forms.
- Review Sheet PDF
- • In the automated world, the Review Sheet PDF will not be generated during the Signoff Reviewer stop.  It will only be generated by the MasterCheck_IR macro so please be sure to run the macro if you want the PDF.
- Streamlined Workflow Step Details Grid
- The grid displayed on the My Deals > Automation tab has been streamlined to only show the steps (in order) and the status of each.
- In order to get the details of each step, expand the step’s Step Report, as mentioned above.

- Setup Updates
- Exclude Automation from Deal Setup Copy From iTracker #16907 – SME: Neemit Desai
- As mentioned before, in order to automate a deal, 1) a workflow template must be assigned to it and 2) the “Opt-in Automation” setting must be enabled.
- To prevent mismatch of such settings, the Deal Setup > Basic Info > Copy From feature will not copy over the ”Opt-in Automation” setting
- Workflow Setup UI (Automation)
- Workflow templates and steps can now be setup on deals via the My Deals > Processing > Workflow tab.
- Processing Method
- The processing method determines how iManage will run through the workflow steps that are enabled on the deal.  By default, automated deals will be set to Manual.
- Manual – similar to the legacy way of signing off, the signoff button in the My Deals > Automation tab must be clicked for each workflow step
- Local Automation – once the deal team is comfortable that each step does what it’s supposed to do for their deal, they may change the processing method to Local Automation.
- After hitting Begin Workflow, each step will progress automatically as long as there are no fails. o Users must still attend to iManage in order to complete the user forms that may pop.
- The workflow will stop once it gets to the Deliver Final Reports step and the processing method will switch to Manual.
- ▪ Again, this is to remind the deal teams to review the deal prior to sending.
- Cloud Automation – is not yet integrated so not applicable at this time.
- Templates
- Templates can only be assigned by the NewBiz team or Senior Managers (with input from shelf SMEs)
- Each template has a set of mandatory steps that must be processed as shown below.  However, only the highlighted steps have been integrated at this time, so only the Classic template should be used.
- Adding a template to a deal will activate the required steps associated with the template • Required steps will be greyed out because they cannot be disabled
- Copy From
- Once a template is assigned to a deal, if the shelf SME or deal team wants to copy the steps enabled from another similar deal, they can use the Copy From feature.
- The deal to Copy From must have at least the same steps assigned to it.  If the deal  to Copy From has less steps than is currently enabled on the loaded deal, the request will fail.
- Only automated deals will appear in the dropdown list.
- Additional Steps
- After a template is assigned to a deal, if deal teams want to enable any of the other integrated steps to be done through automation, they can select those steps.
- Additional step selection is open to all users.
## Notes
- If a deal is currently running through workflow steps, you will not be able to make any changes to this setup.
- Any changes to a deal’s workflow setup will only be applied on a new workflow queue o Ex. If a deal has already gone through Processor Signoff through automation and the deal team decided to add the Check Remit step to the deal’s workflow, deal team must revert the period’s workflow back to Begin Workflow (which will create a new workflow queue including the most recent setup changes).
- Processing Updates
- Optimize spRptBondRatings iTracker #16924
- The Bond Ratings page was previously taking up to 4 minutes to generate on its own.  The report sproc was optimized to only take a few seconds to generate.
- This applies mostly to CMBS deals so you should see a noticeable improvement when running Auto Report on those deals going forward.
- Loaded FileID not Disabled
- • FileIDs that were loaded successfully weren’t displayed as such as the Data-Actions > Process > Import tab.  This bug was fixed – loaded FileIDs will be highlighted in blue.
- Remove Auto Report @ Accept Data Feature
- In the new automation world, Auto Report will be a standalone step that can be assigned preconditions, macros, and pre/post validations.  As such, we would not want the action of Auto Report to be done in conjunction with any other action.
- Therefore, we removed the Auto Report flag next to the Accept Data button in Data-Actions > Process > Discrepancy tab.
- The Auto Report setting in Setup > Collateral Validation tab was also removed.
- Step Check at Auto Report
- Similar to the step checks that were implemented on the Import, Delete, Load, Process and
- Accept Data buttons, a step check was implemented on the Auto Report button on the DataActions > Process > Export tab.
- If the deal has already been sent, you will still be allowed to Auto Report
- If a workflow step is currently being processed, you will be instructed to stop the workflow.
- If any workflow steps have already been completed and the workflow is stopped, you will be warned that all your signoffs will be wiped out.
- Refresh Status after Step Checks
- If a user agrees to continue with wiping previous signoffs during a step check on any of the adhoc buttons mentioned above, the status on top of the screen would still show the old status, which led to confusion.
- The screen will now automatically refresh and display the correct status
- Approval Updates
- Can't pull up prior month reports from imanage. Get Adobe not found error.
- iTracker #16845
- Some software update caused the View Delivered Report by Select Month feature on the My Deals > Processing tab to stop working.  Affected users get an error that iManage “Cannot find Adobe Acrobat Reader on current machine” even if Adobe Reader is installed and working.
- iManage was enhanced to be able to identify the different versions of Adobe that our machines may have installed.
- Optimize Input Manager Calculations iTracker #16921 – SME: Mike Ortiz
- • Input Manager was taking longer than usual to load its calculated values for deals (if a lot of SEI transactions are found) so it was optimized for faster loading.
- Workflow Steps (Automation)
- Signoff - Looksee
- AKA Final Reviewer Signoff was integrated into the workflow process.
- This step will always be a manual step.  Ex. If a deal is using Local Automation and the workflow is able to go through all prior steps without error, the method will change to Manual and the workflow will stop.
- The step will go through all the required checks and validations, but the assigned Looksee will be expected to manually review the deal to ensure nothing was missed.
- Signoff Enhancements
- Signoff - Reviewer
- When preliminary reports and the payment report is delivered at Signoff – Reviewer, iManage will populate the My Deals > Investor Files tab with the pertinent file paths. There was a bug for automated deals where the FilePath was being populated with “/tmp/tdrive/ISERV/@Exports...” instead of "T:/ISERV/@Exports...".  The FilePath will now display the correct drive name.
- Input Manager – Unlock Inputs
- Along with wiping out related signoffs, Unlock Inputs will revert the deal’s workflow to the appropriate step.
- If the Processor unlocks inputs, the Automation tab’s workflow will automatically be reverted back to the Signoff – Processor step.
- If the Reviewer unlocks inputs, the Automation tab’s workflow will automatically be reverted back to the Signoff – Reviewer step.

## From <https://sharepoint.usbank.com/teams/gsf/ir/GSF%20IR%20Release%20Notes/New%20iManage%20Version% 207.0.0.3.docx>
- Version 7.0.0.1 (Release Date: 12/7/2021
- Tuesday, March 7, 2023	3:58 PM
- Automation

- NOTE: Impacted business group for all items is GSF Investor Reporting.  Additional impacted business groups are listed under applicable items.
- Automation
### After many months and a tremendous effort by the Capex team, we have deployed the first phase of automation into Production.   A select few deals will be automated to ensure that the cloud-based processing works as expected.  The following enhancements were implemented as part of this effort:
- Setting up a deal for automation
- Workflow Templates
- Deals are assigned from a number of automation templates, including Bond, CMBS, Bond with Reprocessing, Classic, Collateral, etc.
- Currently, templates can only be assigned to deals by TOS via SQL
- In the future, templates will be assigned by the NewBiz team or Senior Managers (with input from shelf SMEs)
- "Opt-In" for Automation
- Once a deal is assigned an automation template, deal teams must enable the “Opt-in Automation” setting via Deal Setup > Other Settings
- If the deal does not have a template assigned to it, you will not be able to opt the deal into automation.
- If the deal is eligible for the opt-in, you will be warned that if you already started a period’s signoffs using the legacy method, those signoffs will be wiped out.  This will only apply to periods that haven’t been sent yet.
- o Similarly, if you disable the opt-in, any signoffs already started by the automation process will be wiped out and you must start over with the legacy signoff method.
- Automated Indicator
- • Once a deal is assigned a template and opts-in, iManage will display its “Automated” status throughout the application, on every screen.
- Filter for Automated Deals
- On the My Deals screen, there is a new filter that allows you to display only your automated deals (or not).
- You can also set your default view to include the Automated filter under Action > User Startup Preference.
- Automation Tab
- Once a deal is automated, the Automation tab on the My Deals screen will be activated.
- The legacy signoff, Macros and Clicked by Mistake buttons on the Processing tab will be disabled.  However, all the other features on the Processing tab will continue to work as normal.
- This initial iteration of the Automation tab will display the deal’s workflow steps and its own signoff button.
- o The steps listed will be based on the template and any additional steps enabled for the deal.
- Workflow Steps
- At this time, the following steps have been integrated in the automation process (with more to come).
- File Load
- As soon as one file is imported for the deal/period, whether or not it has a FileID, the File Load step will show as "In Progress"
- Once all of the deal's Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs have been loaded, the File Load step will show as “Success”.
- The status of this step will not take into account Optional (Not- Expected) FileIDs
- Begin Workflow (fka Received)
### Currently, the only way to commence a deal’s workflow is for a user to manually hit the Begin Workflow button. o If deal has any Required FileIDs not yet loaded for the period, it will fail with error:
### If all of the deal's Required FileIDs have been loaded, but not all of its Optional (Expected) FileIDs, user will get a pop-up message:
- If Yes, workflow will begin.
- If No, hard stop and status remains at "In Progress".
- If deal doesn't have any FileIDs setup, users will not be stopped from beginning the workflow.
- Eventually, workflow will be able to kick off automatically once all Required and Optional (Expected) FileIDs are imported.
- If a deal continues to not have any Required FileIDs setup, the deal team must continue to manually begin the deal’s workflow.
- Just as we currently have at Received, there is a Large Wire check at Begin Workflow.
- Process Data
- Instead of going to the Data-Actions screen to manually hit the Process Data button, the same process can now be done as part of the workflow.
- It uses the same logic as the old ad-hoc button so if there are no discrepancies or issues, there is no need to switch over to the old screen.
- If there are issues, the error will be displayed in the Workflow Status form.
- All of the calculations and actions called by Process Data are now being done in the cloud.
- Accept Data
- Similarly, instead of going to the Data-Actions screen to manually hit the Accept Data button, the same process can now be done as part of the workflow.
- It uses the same logic as the old ad-hoc button so if there are no discrepancies or issues, there is no need to switch over to the old screen.
- If there are issues, the error will be displayed in the Workflow Status form.
- All of the calculations and actions called by Accept Data are now being done in the cloud.
- Expected Remit Check
- This is a new step that compares the iManage-calculated total remittance amount (after collateral data is finalized) to the wire amount that the Servicer reports in their remittance file.
- If your deal is setup to utilize a data scrubbing/mining tool that can pull the servicer’s remittance amount and loads that into tblServRemitPeriodic, this step can be enabled to verify the wire amount systematically.
- If the amounts differ by more than $5, the step will fail.
- Processor Signoff
- The order of events in the workflow Processor Signoff is slightly different from the legacy Processor Signoff.
- It will first import the payment/tax data from the distrib via a cloud process.
- o Note: It disregards the importing method enabled in Deal Setting > Other Settings, i.e. it no longer opens the distrib on your machine nor use the SSIS method of importing payment/tax data.
- Then, it will display all the pertinent user forms that you need to interact with, such as the Large Wire, Late or Termination forms.
- Lastly, it will run through all the normal checks, such as lock status, populated inputs, cert setup, insurance claims and swap notifications.
- A new check was added to help catch large wires.  Even if a deal “skips” the Large Wire check in the deal settings, if the servicer’s remittance amount is loaded into  tblServRemitPeriodic, iManage will double-check if that amount is greater than $50 million and will email the Cash Analyst assigned to the deal.
- If there are issues with any of the checks, the error will be displayed in the Workflow Status form.
- Reviewer Signoff
- Similar to Processor Signoff, the review/trigger data will be imported first, then all pertinent user forms will appear on your iManage, followed by the rest of the usual Reviewer Signoff checks done via the cloud.
- If there are issues with any of the checks, the error will be displayed in the Workflow Status form.
- Final Delivery Signoff (fka Send)
- Even if the workflow is automated, discussed below, the workflow will stop at the Final Delivery Signoff step in order to remind users that they must review everything before proceeding with sending the final reports.
- All pertinent user forms will appear first, such as Selective File Delivery and Third Party Delivery Confirmation.
- Then it will run through all the usual checks for Send via the cloud, such as master check, discrepancies between the distrib and reviewsheet, incomplete input manager, etc.
- If there are issues with any of the checks, the error will be displayed in the Workflow Status form.
- Workflow Features
- Processing Method
- In the My Deals > Automation tab, there is a drop-down that shows the processing method selected for the deal.  By default, deals will be set to Manual.
- Manual – similar to the legacy way of signing off, the signoff button must be clicked for each workflow step
- Once a step is complete, user will have to manually Close the Workflow Status form opened for that step.
- Local Automation – once the deal team is comfortable that each step does what it’s supposed to do for their deal, they may change the processing method to Local Automation.
- After hitting Begin Workflow, each step will progress on its own as long as there are no fails.
- Users must still attend to iManage in order to complete the user forms that may pop.
- As mentioned above, the workflow will stop once it gets to the Final Delivery Signoff step and the processing method will switch to Manual.
- Again, this is to remind the deal teams to review the deal prior to sending.
- o Cloud Automation – is not yet integrated so not applicable at this time.
- Revert To
- Similar to the legacy Clicked by Mistake, there is a Revert To feature that allows you to revert the deal’s workflow to the desired previous step with one click.
- While a workflow is in progress, the Revert To buttons are disabled and a tool tip is available instead that states that the workflow must be stopped before you can use the feature.
- Once workflow is stopped/failed, the Revert To buttons will be activated next to each completed step.  If clicked, you will be asked if you’re sure you want wipe out your signoffs.
- Stop
- If a deal is going through Local Automation, users must hit the Stop button and confirm the stop in order to prevent the workflow from automatically moving onto the next step.
- Note: the workflow will continue moving along until you confirm that you want to stop the workflow.  This was added in case of an accidental click of the Stop button.
- Once confirmed, iManage will finish the step it is on.  Once the step is done, then the workflow will actually stop.
- Workflow Status Form
- As mentioned above, the Workflow Status form will display the progress of the workflow and any error messages.
- In Manual mode, it will only display the current step’s progress/status.
- In Local Automation mode, it will display every step’s progress/status.
- It is a standalone form so you may navigate to other parts of iManage and it will stay open until you hit Close.
- Step Check with Ad-Hoc Buttons
- In the automated world, data would be imported via loaders and the data would be processed by the deal’s workflow, i.e. there wouldn’t be a need to go to the Data-Actions screens unless there is a problem.
- Suppose you received revised data and don’t realize the deal is automated and going through the workflow.  You go to Data-Actions, out of habit, to hit Delete and Import.
- There are now checks in place on the Delete, Import, Load buttons on the Process and Line Item Adjustments tab and the Process and Accept Data buttons on the Discrepancy tab.
- If the deal has already been sent, you will be instructed to revise the deal
- If a workflow step is currently being processed, you will be instructed to stop the workflow.
- If any of the workflow steps have already been completed and the workflow is stopped, you will be warned that all your signoffs will be wiped out.
- However, if you are importing comments into tblCMSAComment or vwAgencyBreachReview, it will not wipe out your Processor and Reviewer signoffs.
- Enhanced Revision Logic
- When revising a deal due to the Servicer, we would expect to get new periodic files.  If the deal is automated, iManage will reset the period’s workflow back to the File Load step.
- If revising for any other reason, iManage will only reset the workflow back to the first enabled step after Auto Report, since there is no need to reprocess the collateral.
- o If you do need to reprocess collateral data, you can simply Revert To Begin Workflow.
- Setup/Processing Updates
- Process and Accept Data – Cloud-based Processing *
- The actions tied to the Process and Accept Data buttons in Data-Actions > Process > Discrepancy screen are now being done in the cloud.
- From an end-user standpoint, you shouldn’t notice any major difference.  However, you will notice that error messages appear in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen.
- You should be able to resolve all discrepancies or issues as you normally would.
- Mismatched/missing loans and Paidoff Code Violation files will be exported to the T: deal folder by the cloud.
- If you run into unusual errors with either of these features, please escalate them immediately.
- Allocations: Tax- clearing out names iTracker #15313 – SME: Carrie Reynolds
- Fixed bug that wiped out deal allocations for tax duties whenever a role was reassigned.
- Reporting Updates
- New iManage exported loan level file for CMAT shelf iTracker #16775 – SME: Tammy Tam
### A new loan level file was created, with the following fields:
- Reminder that you can setup the loan level files to be exported at the same time as Auto Report, and to any location you choose
- 3 additional fields be added to LL file iTracker #16789 – SME: Dona Werth
- The TOWD loan level file was updated to include the following fields: o Updated AVM Value o Updated AVM Date o Updated AVM Confidence Score
- CMBS modification sub-report iTracker #15677 – SME: Samir Ghia
- A new sub-report named “Repurchases and Modifications” that calculates rolling 12-month balances for loans less than 90 day delinquent is available for the Remittance (Extended)
- Summary

- NOTE: Impacted business group for all items is GSF Investor Reporting.  Additional impacted business groups are listed under applicable items.
- Setup/Processing Updates
- * Capex enhancements.  SMEs: Linda Mai and Neemit Desai
- SQL File Handling *
### After the release of SQL importing for Line Items (Map 16), we ran into issues if the source file had:
- Blank rows/columns preceding the import range
- A different tab was active. Ex. If the file was last saved on the “Mod” tab, Map 16 would be unable to pull the data from the “Line Items” tab.
- The SQL import feature is now able to handle both scenarios
- Map 16 Import Incomplete for CMBS deals *
- When importing into tblLineItems for CMBS deals, a post-import sproc needs to be run to ensure the CollatKey is recorded for the loans and reflected correctly in the Collateral/Remittance Summary
- This was previously only run if importing via the Line Item Adjustments tab
### Now the post-import sproc will also be run if loading the CMBS line items via:
- Data-Actions > Import tab > Import button o Data-Actions > Import tab > Load button o Use Excel macro “LoadiMap_IR”
- Handle Commas in Data *
- Previously, the SQL import feature was unable to correctly load data with commas in a cell of the source file o Example: COL008 of a CMBS Property file
- It would data delimit the data and throw an error that the “file has blank column headers”
- This bug is fixed and SQL imports should only fail due to true format/data issues
- Generic Message When Any Service Down *
- With Capex, many “cloud-based” services will be invoked and, although unlikely, they may go down
- For example, if the File Watcher or Import Service goes down, we would not want users to continually try to import (via a SQL map) needlessly
- If a service goes down, when you invoke it, you will receive the following message: "An automated service is failing.  GSF IR IT has already been notified.  Please wait for further instructions." o As the message states, we have a process in place to immediately notify our IT group if a service goes down or is about to reach capacity so they can address it right away
- In this case, there is no need to submit an iTracker or ITSC ticket to report the issue o Either the GSF IR IT or Support group will notify the business line once the service is back up and running.
- Add tblImportFileSetup to DMT
- iTracker #15695 – SME: Mike Ortiz
- Many people are excited to use the new FileID feature, but requested a way to setup them up in bulk.  Therefore, we have added tblImportFileSetup to the Data Management tool (DMT).
- Can still setup them up individually in Data-Actions > Setup > Servicer Setup > Import File Setup section
- If you have access to Modify/Insert data via the DMT, you have access to this table
### The following fields are required to setup a FileID via the DMT:
- FileID - Any number, ex. “1” (it will automatically be updated once the record is inserted into the table)
- FileName - Name (using the following naming conventions) to help you quickly understand what the FileID represents for your deal.
- The File Name cannot be duplicated within the same deal.
- Note: This is NOT the actual name of the file that you import.
### Standard file naming conventions:
- LoanLev
- LoanLevOcwen
- Mod
- ModSPS
- HampMod
- LineItems
- Delinq
- Sales
- Purch
- Price
- Advance
- Transfer
- DID o MapID– MapID used to import the file.
- Is not limited to what is associated with the deal under Deal Maps.
- Can be any SQL or SSIS map (NOT hardcoded)
- Can be used for multiple FileIDs within the same deal.  However, the File Name you assign to the FileID must be different.
- Inactive - 0
- UpdatedBy – Your preferred ID
### UpdatedDate – Date you’re inserting the record o File Type:
- Required – file that must be loaded every month.  Ex. Servicer’s periodic file
- Optional_Expected – file that isn’t required, but still expected every month.  Ex. Line items
- Optional_NotExpected – file that isn’t needed every month, but may need to be imported on the rare occasion
- File Default Location – does not need to be filled out, but if the file name is consistent, you can populate this field using our standard file masks.
- Ex. M:\{FOLDER}\DATA\{YYYY}\{M}\{DID}_SupportRemit.xlsx o Be sure to include the file extension (.csv, .xls, .xlsx, etc.) o It is case sensitive
- Note: It does not support wildcards.  For a complete list of all the valid file masks, please refer to the File Mask Legend (posted on Sharepoint’s IR Resource Library).
- Once a FileID is setup, it will be listed in the Process > Import tab under the FileID Import grid and you may begin loading your files directly from there.
- Approval Updates
- New Item tblProcessingDataSetup iTracker #15686 – SME: Mary Vaughan
- • “UnpaidCustodian” was added as a valid tax range item
- Remove check for old payment files iTracker #15681
- At Processor and Reviewer Signoff, iManage had been running a check to ensure the payment range had the correct format/number of characters to conform to the old payment text files.
- If a bond has a negative accrual rate, it would fail the check (hard stop) and deal team would be unable to proceed
- Since we are no longer using the old payment files, we removed the check and signoffs can now move forward

- Import Service/File Watcher
- The first milestone for the Capex project allows for importing files via the “cloud”.  Importing issues is consistently one of the top reported items on our pulse surveys.  With these new features, we now have a way to import data using SQL maps that do not rely on the user’s machine.
- Currently, we import data using SSIS maps, which are hard to understand and susceptible to software updates on our machines.
- SQL maps use basic SQL language, which is easier to read and write. o Eventually, when all SSIS maps are converted to SQL, we won’t have to worry about importing crashing our VDIs because they will all be done in the cloud. o Better error messages – If an import fails, simple explanations are passed on for easier troubleshooting.
- The Line Item Adjustments tab’s Import feature now utilizes a SQL map.  There should be no noticeable difference on how it works.
- If it fails, a black message box will appear on the bottom right corner of iManage o If you miss it, you (as the Importer) and the deal team, will get an automated email notification of the error.
- TOS converted the top 10 most used maps.
- These were thoroughly tested by Neemit Desai, Hoang Pham and Johan Laksmana as part of project testing.
- Before they are officially switched to SQL in Production, Queena Duong and Jack Ho will conduct a final round of testing to ensure they work as expected and there is no disruption to your process. o The business line is responsible for converting the remainder of SSIS maps with Queena and Jack managing that effort.
- LoadMap_IR was updated to work with SQL maps.
- SME: Mike Ortiz o When used, it will send your request to a queue. (Import requests from iManage will take priority) o A File Watcher is triggered, finds the file, and sends it to the Import Service to load. o If your SQL map import request fails, you will receive an email notification with the details (similar to above).
- Setup/Processing Updates
- * Capex enhancements.  SMEs: Linda Mai and Neemit Desai
- Remove Import Month / Add Future Periods to Processing Date *
- Import Month and Check Data features have been removed.  All processes that were previously driven by the Import Month now refer to the selected Processing Date instead.
- The Processing Date dropdown includes future periods.  Simply select the period you want to import data for here (instead of the old Import Month).
- When first navigating to Process > Import tab, the current period will be be shown by default.
- o If you change the period, that period will persist as you move around.
- The deal status will show as “Future” for any period that does not have any data loaded yet, even if it is the current period .
- Enhanced Delete All *
- The Delete All feature previously would not delete from every table listed in the Loaded Data grid.
- It only deleted from tables that were listed in a sproc based on deal type
- Now it will delete data based on ImportID, thereby bypassing the limited SQL table list
### Delete All works on all tables, except for:
- Loan Accounting tables, which were already exceptions
- vwAgencyServ – can’t delete from views since they are a combination of multiple base tables
- tblCMSACollatSummary – this table captures data for the underlying deals of a CMBS Resec.  Therefore, when using Delete All on the actual Resec, it won’t find anything any records under that Resec name.
- Previously, all records would move to the Import Log (Deleted) grid, even though the data wasn’t deleted.  Now both the Loade d Grid and Deleted grids will display more accurate information. o When using Delete All for a deal that loaded into the above-mentioned exception tables, the Loaded Grid will show data in those exception tables are still loaded and all other tables are deleted.
- FileID Setup *
- We have a new way to track all the files that we expect to import each period for each deal.
- Setting up all the FileIDs for a deal and utilizing filemasks allows for quicker importing (less clicks) and better tracking (can see which files are still outstanding). • In Data-Actions > Setup > Servicer Setup > Import File Setup section, click AddNewRow
### The following fields are mandatory to setup a FileID:
### File Type:
- Required – file that must be loaded every month.  Ex. Servicer’s periodic file
- Optional_Expected – file that isn’t required, but still expected every month.  Ex. Line items
- Optional_NotExpected – file that isn’t needed every month, but may need to be imported on the rare occasion
- SNEAK PEAK: In the future, deal processing will automatically kick off if all Required and Optional_Expected FileIDs are imported.  Therefore, it is important that you classify the File Type correctly for each of your files.
- File Name –Name (using the following naming conventions) to help you quickly understand what the FileID represents for your deal.
- The File Name cannot be duplicated within the same deal.
- Note: This is NOT the actual name of the file that you import.
### Standard file naming conventions:
- LoanLev
- LoanLevOcwen
- Mod
- ModSPS
- HampMod
- LineItems
- Delinq
- Sales
- Purch
- Price
- Advance
- Transfer
- o Map– MapID used to import the file.
- Is not limited to what is associated with the deal under Deal Maps.
- Can be any SQL and SSIS map
- • Note: FileIDs cannot be setup for hardcoded maps.
- Can be used for multiple FileIDs within the same deal.  However, the File Name you assign to the FileID must be different.
- File Default Location – does not need to be filled out, but if the file name is consistent, you can populate this field using our standard file masks .
- o Ex. M:\{FOLDER}\DATA\{YYYY}\{M}\{DID}_SupportRemit.xlsx o Be sure to include the file extension (.csv, .xls, .xlsx, etc.) o It is case sensitive o Note: It does not support wildcards.  For a complete list of all the valid file masks, please refer to the File Mask Legend (posted on Sharepoint’s IR Resource Library).
- Inactive – If you no longer need to import a file for the foreseeable future, but don’t want to lose your FileID setup, you can set the record to Inactive.
- Delete – To delete a FileID, simply click on the row and hit the Delete button on top of the grid.
- FileID Import *
- Once a FileID is setup, it will be listed in the Process > Import tab under the FileID Import grid.
- If the File Default Location had been populated with file masks, iManage will automatically interpret those masks in the Default Location field based on the Processing Date selected.
- Click Loadnext to desired FileID to import the file o If iManage finds the file, it will automatically load the file. o If iManage can’t find the file, it will open the Open File dialog box for you to select the file manually.
- Once the file imports successfully, the related FileID will be disabled (highlighted in blue and the Load button will not work) o The Loaded Data grid will display the import information from that FileID load
- To delete the data imported, simply select the record associated with the FileID from the Loaded Data grid and hit Delete. o The FileID will be re-enabled and available for re-import
- Once all of a deal’s FileIDs are setup, there should be no need to use the old Import Data Source and Import feature.
- o SNEAK PEAK: Only deals setup and loading with FileIDs will be eligible for full automation.
- Line Item Adjustments *
- As mentioned above, the Line Item Adjustments tab was updated to use a new importing method, but there should be no noticeabl e difference to the end user.
- MapID 16, which is called by the Import button, was converted to a SQL map.
- TIP! Ensure the correct period is listed in the import file.  For example, even if August is chosen on screen, if the file says 6/1/2021, it will load/overwrite data for 6/1/2021
- If line items were loaded via a FileID, this tab will reflect that data o If deleting all data that was loaded via a FileID from the Line item tab, the FileID will be available again for a re-import.
- Assuming MapID 16 was setup as a FileID for your deal, this tab should only be used for ad-hoc/additional imports of line items.
- If the deal has a FileID associated with MapID 16, loading line items from this tab will NOT be considered a successful load of the FileID.
- If you click on the Template button, you will notice that the blank rows/columns in the template were removed.
- Updated Map Screens *
- The map screens were updated to work with SQL maps
- DynamicMaptab – The ETL column shows whether a map is SSIS or SQL
- Mapping Screen – after double-clicking on a map, you can view that map’s logic.
### If the map is SQL, you can access a field’s SQL_Property by clicking on the box on the right side of the cell:
- fmSqlPropertywill open o All users can view SQL logic, but only users with EditMaps rights have the ability to change SQL logic
- New Map – When creating a new map using the “Save to New Map” button, the New Map form will open.
- We removed the word “DTS” from the form to avoid confusion.  o Can be used to create new SQL maps.
- Map Column History – when clicking on the History button for a field, the Map Column History form will show both the old SSIS or SQL logic changes
- Email Notifications of SQL Map Import Failures *
- If an import fails on a SQL map, the Importing Engine will send you an email with the error details.
- The email will come from “iManageNoReply@usbank.com”
- Bayview Map Checks
- iTracker #15452 – SME: John Kavlich
- Certain Bayview deals need to use certain maps and Remittance Summaries.
- In order to prevent bad reporting, new checks have been added to Accept Data to notify you if you are most likely using the w rong map or Remittance Summary.
- If you get this notification, please reach out to Mary Vaughn and/or John Kavlich.
- Sample Package Tracking
- iTracker #13792 – SME: Mike Ortiz
- Previously, individual report pages were tracked the same way for Sample and normal Final Packages.  Consequently, packaging would get mixed up.
- Now, individual pages of the Sample Package is tracked separately.
- Report Updates
- Hist Liq Loss Loan Detail page - Freddie CMBS RL reporting incorrect iTracker #15570 – SME: Yuan Li-Crouch
- The Freddie version of the Historical Liquidation Loss Loan Detail report was updated to tie to the Freddie version of the Historical Bond/Collateral Realized Loss Reconciliation page.
- Previously, the report shared the logic of the normal CMBS version, but wouldn’t tie whenever there was additional recoveries/losses on a loan.
- Optional Sales Report needs to be generated even if there is no OS iTracker #15497 – SME: Irina Markevich
- The Optional Sale Report (used with RESECs) previously had gridlines that didn’t convert nicely in the Excel version of the f ile so it was revamped with no more gridlines.
- Additionally, the client requested that the report be generated even if there is no Optional Sales for the period.

- iTracker #15385 – SME: Mike Ortiz
- Added a column to tblSetup called "FirstPeriod".  This can be used when the month of the first PERIOD does not match the month of the first PAYMENT DATE.
- Example: First period of Feb 2021, with a first payment date of 3/1/2021.
- Managers can populate this field via the DMT, as needed.  In the example above, the FirstPeriod would be populated with "2/1/2021".
### The FirstPeriod field only needs to be populated if the deal does not fall into one of these categories:
- Payment date always in the same month as the current period, ex.2/25/2021 (Feb 2021) o Payment date always falls in the month following the current period, ex.3/3/2021 (Feb 2021) o If neither of the above is true, such as when the second payment (3/29) is within the same month as the first payment date (3/1), the FirstPeriod field will need to be populated in order for the Cover Page of the statement to report the correct Distribution Date.

### For deals assigned to you as the Processor or Reviewer, if you have the deal loaded anywhere in iManage/iServ, when you go back to My Deals, the deal should be loaded with you as the Analyst:
- If you had the deal loaded in the My Deals screen, go to another screen and come back,
- My Deals should still be loaded on the same deal under your own view o If you had sorted your view of the My Deals screen by something, switching to another screen and back to My Deals should keep that sort order in place
### For deals not assigned to you, if you have the deal loaded anywhere in iManage/iServ, when you go back to My Deals:
- iManage should be smart enough to know what deal was last loaded within the application and keep that deal loaded no matter what screen you go to
- Only once you load a new deal on any screen should it switch to another deal
- Reviewer Signoff and Send check
- iTracker #13738 – SME: Neemit Desai
- There was an incident when a Processor had signed off, which meant the Reviewer's allocations indicated the deal was ready for Reviewer Tasks and signoff so the Reviewer did so.  However, during this time, the Processor Clicked by Mistake to redo some work without the Reviewer knowing.  Since the Reviewer didn’t refresh her screen, she was able to sign off on the deal and Send it.
- Added checks to the Reviewer Signoff, Final Reviewer Signoff and Send buttons to error out and automatically refresh the user’s view if any prior signoffs were wiped out.
- Fix Multi Process Feature Specifically for Create Package
- Report
- iTracker #15218 – SME: Brian Scheff
- For deals that are setup to use the Create Package Report macro via the Macro manager in one of its steps, such as Process Distrib, if multiple deals are selected and the Multi Process feature is used, the wrong DID parameter may pass through during the packaging.  The result was the headers in the Final Packages were generated with different DIDs.
- The Multi Process feature was updated to pass through the DID parameter better, specifically when it comes to packaging reports.
- If you use this feature, please pay close attention to the deal name on each page of the package and report any anomalies.
- Fix Insurance Claims Email Notification Logic
- iTracker #15245 – SME: Ruby Liu
- When hitting Processor Signoff, iManage automatically checks to see if any insurance claims amounts had changed and, if so, emails the Admin of revised amounts.
- However, the “Revised” emails were not being sent if the prior or current claim was $0.
- The logic has been fixed to send out the “Revised” email if the current claims simply do not match the prior claims.
- Add Fields to Tax table
- iTracker #13902 – SME: Mike Ortiz
- Added two new fields to tblProcessingData (i.e. tax range) – ItemLabel and ItemType
- Since we expect to use these new fields for various things in the future, we are making it the default method for importing this data
- NOTE: This will not be required/used any time soon.
- However, since this isn’t being used immediately, all deals will have the “Use Old Tax Range Method” setting enabled in Other Settings when this is released
- There are a handful of deals that already import the payment and tax ranges via SSIS package – those with hundreds of CUSIPs and used to take 30 minutes to signoff
- For those deals, since the SSIS method is now the default method, we are removing the Other Setting option of “SSIS Import Payment Info Method” o If your deal previously used the “SSIS Import Payment Info Method”, please reach out to Mike Ortiz or Linda Mai to convert to the new “data” range method

- First Period vs First Distribution Date
- SME: Mike Ortiz
- Some newer deals pay 5+ business days after the 25th which means the current month’s payment actually falls in the following month
- Example: FirstKey RT 2020-C2 o First period was July, whose first payment was on August 3rd o Payment date calculator worked fine o Could process in iServ for July fine
- Issue for the first period of these deals o Deal wouldn’t show up in the first period (July) correctly on the My Deals screen o If changed the First Distrib Date so that it would show in July, then the payment date will be incorrect on the My Deals screen and on the reports
- iManage now smart enough to handle these deals as long as the payment date logic is setup correctly, including country codes.  As long as the payment date logic calculates the same date as the actual first payment date, everything will work as it should.
- Using above example, deal will show up on the My Deals screen for the July 2020 period o Data can be processed in the July 2020 period o First payment and distribution dates will generate correctly on reports

- Update RESEC logic for CVR
- iTracker #14075 – SME: Samir Ghia
### There are a few enhancements related to how RESECs are handled in the new CVR Process:
- New setting to use with Internal RESECs based on internal underlying remittance summaries, such as the Bayview RESECs.  (Deals setup in tblResec)
- Note: This feature will not work on RESECs based on internal underlying CUSIPs.
- On the underlying deals, enable the Post-Processing setting called “Auto processing of RESEC after underlying deals are done”.  Do NOT enable it for the RESEC.
- All the UDIDs need to go through the normal process of Process > Accept Data
- Only at Accept Data of the UDIDs will the sproc kick in that automatically updates the Resec status to Finalized.
- Switch to the RESEC and should see the status is “Finalized”
- Note: With this automatic solution, you no longer need to hit Process or Accept Data on the RESEC in order to Auto Report or generate packages
- RESECs with INTERNAL Underlying Cusips – Allows for Partial Acceptance o If some of your underlying data is available, you can now Process your RESEC to reconcile that information.  You will not have to wait for all data to be loaded.
- You will no longer get a “principal reduction check” on the missing UDID(s)
- You will receive a “missing loan” pop-up for the missing UDID(s) instead and a MismatchedLoans file will export to the T: deal folder
- After resolving discrepancies and hitting Accept Data, the status will change to Partial Acceptance
- View/Export Report allowed since at Partial Acceptance (and only for whitelisted files)
- Note: Data will be blank for missing UDID(s).
- RESECs with EXTERNAL Underlying Cusips – Inserts records for $0 CUSIPs o iManage will insert a record in tblLoanMonthly for active $0 CUSIPs in case there are payments on them in the future
- Improve Allocations Screen - Add Filter

- Note: The text box has been removed from the UI.  Please use the filter options instead.
- For Bond/Collateral deals – if a deal is already loaded in iManage, switching to the Allocations screen will automatically filter to that deal.
- o To remove the filter and see all Bond deals, simply click on “Bond” in the service type drop-down
- For Tax, the Tax Location field has been pulled into the grid to make it easier to filter by TaxProcessingLocation
- Whenever new tax entities and duties are added, you can now use the filters (filter by blanks and Tax Location) to quickly find the deals that need to be allocated.
- Add New TIR Codes for UK Deals

- The following new Rate Reset Reports were added to Pivot and iManage: o GBP Rate Set Report – UK Rate Reset Report (TIR Code: 30PDF) o EUR Rate Set Report – UK Rate Reset Report – EUR (TIR Code: 31PDF) o USD Rate Set Report – UK Rate Reset Report – USD (TIR Code: 32PDF)

- The feature that allows us to deliver files to clients at Send stopped working a few months ago and has been fixed

- The field allows for filemasks

- • We now have the ability to customize the month ranges in the Remaining Term stratification table for the Reference Pool Characteristics report via Data-Actions > Settings > Advanced Settings.
- Select the DID in the left panel
- Select the Reporting category in the right panel (or on the left is there are already Reporting items set up on the deal).
- Flag the Stratification checkbox in the right panel and hit Insert
- Select Stratification on the left panel so it’s highlighted orange
- Flag the Subreport Name checkbox in the right panel and UNFLAG the boxes below it.  Hit Insert.
- Select Subreport Name on the left panel so it’s highlighted orange
- Choose the Subreport that you want to customize from the dropdown and hit Update
- Flag the Subreport Step checkbox and specify the range value desired.  Hit Insert.

- PaidOffCode Logic
- SME: Kalan Jablonski
- During testing of the HELOC Loan count project, we realized that iManage was automatically assigning a PaidOffCode of 3 to liquidating loans if they met certain criteria.  However, this was incorrectly setting active $0 HELOC loans as paid off loans.
- This logic has been removed and PaidOffCodes will be determined solely by the maps used to import servicer data.
### At Accept Data, iManage will double-check to make sure that loans that seem to have paid off have all the necessary data points populated:
- o End Bal = 0 o PaidOffCode populated o PaidOffDt populated
- A PaidOffCodeViolation file will generate if any of the above data points are missing.  Please resolve any discrepancies found before moving forward to ensure data integrity.
- TOWD HELOC Loan Counts
- SME: Kalan Jablonski
- To ensure that HELOC loan counts are calculated correctly, historical data needs to be reviewed/fixed and reports regenerated to confirm the counts are updated as expected.
- The first shelf to go through this rigorous review is the TOWD HELOCs.
- Going forward, loan counts on the reporting package for this shelf should reflect the true number of active loans.
- Note: Other HELOC deals will go through the same data and reporting review in the coming months and deployed into Production on a rolling basis.

- iTracker #13865
- iManage automatically creates deal folders and shortcuts for new deals, based on the service enabled on the deals.  However, there was a bug that created these folders/shortcuts on taxonly deals.
- Note: These unnecessary shortcuts were the cause of the M: drive taking so long to load.
### Automatic folder/shortcut creation rules have been updated as follows:
### If a deal is Bond, Collateral or Fund Accounting AND dealfolder field is populated in tblsetup: then check for or create the following:
- Create J: folder and Sub folders (PDF and Support)
- Create M: folder and Sub folders (Data, Docs, Setup, TempSupportFiles)
- Add shortcut to J: deal folder (#1)
- Add shortcut IN the J: deal folder to M: Sub folders (#2)    3. Create T:\iServ\DID and Sub folder (PackagePDF)
- Add shortcut to J:\Deal Name (#1)
- Add shortcut IN the J: deal folder to T:\iServ DID folder
- Add shortcut IN the M: deal folder to T:\iServ DID folder
- If a deal is Backup Servicing, create folder in U:\Backup Servicing named the same as the DID (not tblSetup.DealFolder).
### If a deal has a Tax Service enabled AND Tax Platform = "S", then check create the following:
- 1. T:\Tax folder named as the DID
- Add shortcut IN the J: deal folder to T:\Tax\DID folder (ONLY IF the J: deal folder exists.  If not, skip this)

- Processor Tasks – Crashing/Freezing
- iTracker #13567, 13805, 13810, 13824, 13825, 13853 – SMEs: Samir Ghia / Neemit Desai
### Numerous bugs related to the new Processor Tasks process were fixed:
- Due to bad printer settings, badly formatted reports can be generated and may not be noticed under the old comparison method that only replaced changed data pages.  Therefore, the Final Package task will always be reset with all new pages every time it is regenerated, i.e. no checkmarks will be saved from prior signoffs.
- The prior Final Package and prior Support Package will no longer automatically close when the current Support Package is saved.  Prior packages will remain open until both the current Support Package and current Final Package are check-marked and saved, at which point all the files will automatically close.
- iManage will no longer crash when trying to save the Support Package task for new deals.  Previously, it was looking for prior packages, that didn’t exist, so it would crash. o Note: I’ve added the Support Package task back to the new deals from last month
- iManage will no longer freeze if you accidentally click on iManage (in the background) while the tasks are up.
- The column headers in the Tasks Form have been disabled so that columns will no longer sort or error out if you accidentally click on the headers.
- For those who prefer to continually check-mark and save your work without the tasks closing (old method), you may do so using Show Tasks Form.
- Hit Processor Tasks – after saving the current Support and Final Packages, the files will automatically close.  The Show Tasks Form button will be enabled.
- As long as you haven’t hit Processor Signoff yet, when you click Show Tasks Form, the task form buttons will be “Process”
- You can continue processing each task – checking and saving as much as you like, until you are done.
- If your deal doesn’t have a Support Package, you will not be able to pull up the Prior Package via a task.  However, you can use the Report Folder button on the task form to open the T: drive folder and open the prior package from there. o Once you are done, manually close the file windows and the Tasks Form.
- Once Processor Signoff is complete, as the Processor, when you hit Show Tasks Form, the task buttons will be “View” – you will only be able to view the files for reference.  If you want to make any updates to them, you will either have to Reset the task or hit Clicked By Mistake.
- As the Reviewer or Final Reviewer, once the Processor Tasks are complete, when you hit Show Tasks Form, it will open the Reviewer tasks.

- If a revision is not needed, please re-process the deal anyway.  Please refer to the Restate Reversal Best Practice found on the IR Resource Library for further details.

- Update fnRatingCUSIPs

- fnRatingCUSIPs previously filtered out paid-off CUSIPs.  Consequently, we did not record when rating agencies withdrew ratings for the inactive CUSIPs, as that may occur months after.

- Streamline of Processor Tasks
- iTracker #12195 / PI # 1685 – SME: Samir Ghia
### In an effort to reduce inefficiencies and the number of clicks required when you click on Processor Tasks, the process has been enhanced as follows:
- If the Support Package task is enabled, iManage will check to make sure a current Support Package exists.  If not, it will auto-generate the Support Package for you.
- As soon as iManage finds/creates the Support Package it will automatically open the Task form and two PDFViewer windows. o No longer need to click on any buttons to open the files
- The first window will include three tabs: o Prior period’s marked Support Package o Prior period’s marked Final package
- Current period’s Support Package – you will be able to only save checks made to this file
- Note: if the deal does not have a Support Package task, the first window will open the prior period’s marked Final package for easy reference
- The second window will open the Final Package
- As soon as you checkmark and save both current files, they will automatically close, the Tasks form will close and the signoff button will proceed to Processor Signoff o No need to manually close each window or complete a checklist o Does not matter what order you complete the tasks in
- Use the Show Tasks Form feature to view the completed tasks
- If you need to make additional checks to either file, you will have to either Reset the task or Clicked By Mistake – both of which will roll the process back to Processor Tasks.
- After Processor Signoff is complete, you can use Show Tasks Form to view the files you had approved.  When you hit View, you will get a reminder that if you want to mark the file up further, you will have to Reset the task or Clicked by Mistake.  This is not an error – it is simply an informational / reminder message.
- You will also notice that when viewing an approved file, the stamp tool will not be available since the file is in read only mode.
- Note: Reviewer Tasks will be similarly updated in a few months once everyone is comfortable with the changes that were made to Processor Tasks.
- Setup/Processing Updates
- Refresh Bug: Deal Setup
- iTracker #13710
- If another deal was previously loaded to Deal Setup, using the Quick Search > Setup button for another deal was not refreshing the Deal Setup screens with the new deal's information.  This bug has been fixed.

- iTracker #13569 – SME: Mike Ortiz
- The new packaging process requires that a deal’s process status to be either 'Finalized' or 'Locked'.
- However, hitting Accept Data on various deals was not correctly moving their status forward from “Imported” or “Processed”.  Deal teams would either have to use the old packaging method due to a “Data has not been finalized” error that couldn’t be resolved by re-Accepting Data or run “CR Reports for PDF Package”, even though they had already run Auto Report, in order to use the new packaging method.
- This bug has been fixed and all deals should be able to use the new packaging method without further issues.
- Formerly impacted deal shelves included: o STACR deals o TPMT Master o TPMFT Master o USROF deals
- If you were previously using the old packaging method (enabled under Deal Setup > Other Settings), please disable the setting to use the new packaging method.
- Note: SEC deals that require an HTML version of the final package can also switch to the new packaging method.
- HTML files are generating correctly again when using the Package PDF button.
- At the time of this writing, it was not working when using “Create Package Report” via Macro Manager, but that should be addressed shortly.

## From <https://sharepoint.usbank.com/teams/gsf/ir/GSF%20IR%20Release%20Notes/New%20iManage%20Version% 206.2.2.5.docx>
- Version 6.2.2.4 (Release Date: 12/12/2019)
- Tuesday, March 7, 2023	4:23 PM
- Packaging Enhancement Project (PI #1550 and 1565)
- Note: The project should resolve the issues reported in iTrackers 12413, 12240, 12254.
- The packaging process was overhauled to reduce the time it takes to generate the reporting package.
### Highlights include:
- Creation of the collateral level Crystal reports is now happening at Auto Report, i.e. all nondistrib/external reports
- Loan level data must be processed and accepted before the Crystal reports can be created for the selected month
- If you enabled Auto Report at Accept Data, there is no need to hit Auto Report separately
- All buttons in the Process screens will be disabled to prevent data changing while the reports are being generated
- All other screens will be accessible while Auto Report is running – you can simultaneously work in other Data-Actions screens, switch to another deal, switch to the My Deals screen, etc.
- “CR Reports for PDF Package” – Any changes to the TOC or Crystal reports require them to be regenerated.
- If you have already created your package but need to make a change to the Table of Contents cover page or any of the Crystal reports, use the “CR Reports for PDF Package” in the Run drop-down in the My Deals screen (or Auto Report) to regenerate them.
- Examples include changing the Admin, updated Advanced Settings, adding/removing a report, footnote, etc.
- When you hit Package PDF, iRibbon will generate the distrib reports and will merge all the reports together.
- If the data is not processed in iManage and/or only has distrib and/or external reports, simply hit Package PDF to generate the package.
- The Excel Table of Contents page will now include the bank logo and graphics (if we are the Trustee on the deal)
- Agency Supplemental Zip/Files will automatically be generated after the final package is complete (at Package PDF).  You may notice iManage pause after it states “Creating PDF Package is completed” – it is actually moving on to extracting the supplemental package so please wait.
- You will see new status boxes in the bottom right-hand corner as it’s going through the extract process.
- You can still manually create the supplemental package via the Export > Extract Template button
- Create Sample Package (iTracker #12430) – this Run option has been renamed to reflect the “Sample” watermark that is added to the sample packages.
- Create Sample Package without Watermark – new option added for sample packages required for closing documents of potential new deals. o This feature is locked down to users who work with specific clients.  Managers must submit an iTracker to request access to the feature.
- Deal must have a distrib with the month set to match the month you are generating the package for.
- Deal cannot have any data processed for the month.  The package will generate only deal name, report titles and headers.
- Be Careful!  iRibbon uses the clipboard to create the Excel reports, so if you try to copy and paste something outside of iManage/VDI, you will be pasting a “report” instead of whatever you meant to paste.  Please refrain from using copy and paste while reports are being generated.
- The following update(s) are related to changes to setup/processing.
- Update tblSetup When Updating Processor Allocations (#12408 / PI #1742)
### The Office and ProcessLocation fields in tblSetup are used for certain features and reports but are not actively being updated because they are not visible anywhere within iManage.  These fields will now reflect the office that the assigned Processor works out of.  If the deal is reassigned to a Processor at another office, the following fields will automatically update to reflect the new office:
- tblSetup.Office and tblSetup.ProcessLocation
### IR Processing Location (visible only on the UI):
- The auto update applies to Bond, Collateral, Backup Servicing and Fund Accounting deals.  For Backup deals that don’t have a Processor assigned, the fields will reflect the Reviewer’s location.
- Update cutoffbatch map - for alphanumeric LIDs (#12423) – SME: Keagan Delfosse
- The "UDPATE CUTOFFBATCH" map was updated to allow alphanumeric characters for the "LID" column.
- iServ's Next Net WAC Calc incorrect in February (Interest Reserve Month) (#11782) – SME: Christine Paidosh
- Last February, the NEXT net WAC rate was calculated incorrectly on interest reserve deals that had a payoff in either January or February (AGG AND SUB LEVEL BASIS). The calculation will now correctly add back the interest reserve withheld for the loans that paid off in either month when it calculates the NEXT Net WAC calculation for the month of February.
- trgComLoanSetupOrig Not Working (#12354) – SME: Mike Bae
- In our effort to restrict personal data, maps 1663, 1786, 1787, 1788, and 1789 were updated to no longer allow Property Name, Property Address and Property County to load into our data tables.
- The following update(s) are related to changes to the approval/revision process.
- Input Manager Refresh, check, and export (#12068 / PI#1675) SME: Mike Ortiz
- A new macro is available in MacroManager called "Input Manager". This macro will refresh, check, and export the Input Manager file to the T drive.
- DTC Rate Revision files not generating (#12436) SME: Jae Choi
- When a revision results in payment changes, iManage will resume creating and sending a DTS Revision file to the Admin and Cash Analyst with the File Delivery email notification.  The file stopped generating after the Revision Enhancement project.
- Include SME's in Retraction Notification Email's -- sent out when revised button is used in iManage (# 12411 / PI#1747) SME: Christine Paidosh
- For deals that are associated with a certain shelf in Deal Setup, when they are revised, the Shelf SME will be notified, along with the Admin and Cash Analysts, to improve communication and awareness on things that can affect the shelf.
- Task Force Issue radio button on Revision form (#12395) SME: Jae Choi
- If a revision needs to be escalated to the Issues Task Force, clicking “Yes” to the Task Force Issue section will automatically email the Task Force group with the details so you don’t have to.
### Revision Form - collateral type missing dates in the period selection: related to 12357 (#12409) SME:
- Jae Choi
- The Revision form was not pulling in all the completed periods for collateral deals.  The logic was updated to correctly capture all completed periods.
- The following updates are miscellaneous enhancements.
- STACR Agency deal archive to prior month and current month (#12392, 12447 & 12458) - SME: Brian Scheff
- Each Agency deal can easily have 100k+ loans and the storing of this data progressively slowed down our database.  We will now automatically archive all tblAgency% monthly tables beyond the prior month at the beginning of each month.  This will keep our database as lean as possible, which benefits all deals.
- Inquiry Tracker escalation emails (#12428) - SME: Samir Ghia
- Inquiry Tracker escalation emails to the Issues Task Force was providing incorrect information.  This bug has been fixed.
- DMT - tblPmtDay tblSetup field lockdown (#12200) – SME: Neemit Desai
- To be consistent with the security put in place on the Deal Setup UI fields for Due Date and Inactive flag, the same fields are now locked down so that only Managers and up can view and modify the fields through the DMT.
- DataManagement tool - Modify or Delete doesn't work for tblSDIDCrossReference (#12077) TblSDIDCrossReference was not setup correctly for the DMT in Production.  The setup has been fixed.
- Delete – the Delete tab, within the file that opens with the Modify feature, should work correctly now.
